raw.title: Senior Embedded Android Engineer- Hardware
raw.description:
Team description

SumUp's Hardware Development team builds the physical products millions of small businesses rely on every day, and this role sits right at the start of a new chapter: moving our in-house hardware onto the Android platform for the first time. This isn't a typical Android device, it's a highly customised, security-first product built from scratch, which means the person joining will help define how the operating system, drivers, and secure processor come together rather than inheriting someone else's setup. The team works closely with hardware, software, and QA engineers across the bring-up process, so this role offers a rare chance to shape a product's foundations while working alongside experienced embedded and secure processor leads.

What you'll do

  • Support system bring-up for the new Android embedded platform, from bootloader through to kernel and framework
  • Integrate and maintain kernel modules and drivers, including power management and connectivity components
  • Contribute to build system integration across the platform
  • Debug hardware and software issues at the protocol level and help resolve critical issues found during testing
  • Carry out testing and validation to confirm the platform is stable and secure before release

You'll be great for this role if…

  • Experience developing embedded systems with a strong focus on Android OS, gained over several years in a professional setting
  • Strong knowledge of the Android OS architecture, from bootloader (U-Boot, Little Kernel) and kernel through to framework and services
  • Hands-on experience debugging hardware interfaces at protocol level, including I2C, SPI, UART, and SDIO
  • Solid understanding of embedded security concepts such as Secure Boot, TrustZone (TEE), dm-verity, encryption, and hardware-backed key storage
  • Comfort working with Qualcomm Snapdragon or MediaTek platforms, and expert-level C programming for embedded Linux environments

Why you should join SumUp

🌎 Opportunity to work with SumUppers globally on large-scale fintech products used by millions of businesses worldwide, from our Berlin office. This involves an office-first setup 

🌈 Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: be part of a workplace that values and promotes diversity, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone's perspectives are respected and embraced 

🚀 Enrolment onto our Virtual Stock Option programme: you will own a stake in SumUp's future success 

📚 A dedicated annual L&D budget of €2000 for your individual development, which can be used to attend conferences and/or advance your career through further education 

💶 A corporate pension scheme where we match up to 20% of your contributions 

🏖 Generous time off: enjoy 28 days of paid leave plus public holidays and special leave days 

🌈 Numerous other benefits such as Urban Sports Club subsidy, Kita placement assistance, subsidised office lunches 

🌴 Break4me: 1-month sabbatical after 3 years of service 

🔗 Referral Bonus: earn additional rewards by referring talented individuals to join the SumUp team

About SumUp

Be empowered to do more that matters.

At SumUp, we're on a mission to empower small businesses across the globe by providing simple and affordable tools that allow them to thrive. Today, over 4 million businesses in 38 markets rely on SumUp as their financial partner to manage payments, finance and customer relationships.

Our commitment to small businesses is reflected in our diverse team of over 3,000 SumUppers from over 90 nationalities, united by global collaboration and an innovative mindset. Our core values lay the foundation for who we are and what we stand for, shaping our work culture and driving our success. We foster inclusivity and a continuous learning culture, providing a safe space for personal and professional growth. Our differences make us unique and strong as we strive to create an environment where everyone belongs and feels supported, no matter how they identify.

SumUp is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer, actively seeking and embracing diversity in our workforce. We don't make hiring or employment decisions based on race, colour, religion or religious belief, ethnic or national origin, nationality, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age or any other basis protected by applicable laws or prohibited by company policy. Our commitment extends beyond recruitment to creating a safe and respectful workplace where harassment of any form is strictly prohibited. Discover more about our culture and opportunities on our careers website, and follow our journey on LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok.

raw.description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Team

DashOS is DoorDash's merchant technology platform. It brings together the products restaurants and local businesses use to run their own business, sell on their own channels and keep their guests coming back, including online ordering, websites and apps, and loyalty. DashOS connects these tools with the demand and growth learnings of the DoorDash, Wolt and Deliveroo marketplaces, so merchants can grow both on our marketplaces and on their own channels.

In EMEA, we are building DashOS market by market. The team is small and works like a startup within the larger DoorDash. When joining DashOS, you will help shape a new business from an early stage: what we offer merchants to fuel their growth, how we take it to market and how we support merchants once they are live.

Our Strategy & Operations team builds the DashOS business end to end in EMEA: what we focus on, how we measure success, and the playbooks that make growth repeatable. We work in small cross-functional pods that find improvement opportunities, launch and iterate, together with Product, Engineering, Analytics, Finance, Legal, Marketing, our merchant and consumer teams.

About the Role

We are now looking for a Senior Manager, Revenue Operations to build the commercial engine behind DashOS. You will own the systems, numbers and operating rhythm that turn a multi-product strategy into predictable revenue, across all DoorDash, Wolt and Deliveroo markets in EMEA.

What you'll be doing

As the Senior Manager, Revenue Operations for DashOS EMEA, you will partner directly with DashOS commercial leadership to co-own the go-to-market plan and run the operating cadence for the sales and account management teams selling DashOS. This is a senior individual contributor role for a builder: you will set up the tracking and planning foundations, then use them to make the sales organisation measurably better.

Day-to-day in this role you'll:

  • Build the revenue tracking infrastructure: own our CRM setup and the data flows into our BI stack, so pipeline, activities and revenue for every DashOS product live in one place
  • Run the commercial operating cadence, including pipeline tracking, pacing and weekly forecasting with sales and account managers, and own the DashOS commercial narrative to EMEA leadership
  • Own sales planning across markets: set targets and quotas through bottom-up and top-down allocation, and design books of business, territories and coverage models that match our growth goals
  • Turn sales performance data into action by building dashboards that act as the single source of truth for account-level performance and risk, and surfacing insights that managers and sellers can act on
  • Design and roll out incentive systems, including MBOs, SPIFFs and variable compensation, together with Finance, so sales and account managers own DashOS revenue alongside marketplace revenue
  • Make DashOS part of the core commercial motion, so it shows up in every account manager's book of business, account plans and business reviews rather than running on the side
  • Automate and scale with AI, removing manual work for sellers and managers (e.g. pre-populated account plans, automated pipeline views) so teams spend their time with merchants

Our humble expectations

  • Significant experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Strategy & Operations or a similar commercial role, ideally in a fast-growing tech company. A management consulting background is a plus.
  • A track record in sales planning: quota and target setting, territory and book-of-business design, and forecasting cadences for a multi-market sales organisation.
  • Hands-on with data and systems. You are comfortable with SQL and BI tools (e.g. Looker, Tableau) and have worked deeply in a CRM such as Salesforce. You build things yourself rather than only writing specs.
  • Experience designing incentive models, variable pay structures, SPIFFs and performance tracking across commercial teams.
  • A builder and generalist who is comfortable with ambiguity, can take a broad mandate and turn it into concrete outputs, and doesn't need a fully built stack to deliver.
  • A clear communicator and trusted partner to senior leaders, able to translate data into a commercial narrative and build alignment across Sales, Finance and Product.
  • Strong understanding of distinct sales motions, including Enterprise Sales, SMB Sales and Account Management. Experience with multi-product or platform sales is a plus.
  • Bonus: experience using AI and automation to scale commercial operations.

Why join us

You will do work that matters and help build one of DoorDash's next big bets. Working here, you can expect to:

  • Make a visible impact every day, directly improving how merchants run and grow their business.
  • Learn fast in an entrepreneurial environment, with autonomy, pace and real responsibility.
  • Build a career, not just a role, as DashOS grows across EMEA.
  • Deliver together in an inclusive, diverse and values-driven culture, with big hearts and small egos.

Next steps

If you are excited about building a new business from an early stage and taking real ownership, click below to apply, add your CV and get the conversation going! We review applications on an ongoing basis. 💙

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. Du führst unsere 2 Senior Fleet Technicians, 5 Regional Fleet Manager und damit indirekt die Fleet Manager, Techniker:innen und Schadensexpert:innen an über 40 Stationen in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz. Du berichtest direkt an unseren Business Director DACH und bist Teil des DACH-Leadership-Teams. Was dich erwartet: ein schnell wachsendes Unternehmen, ein junges, motiviertes Team und viel, das noch aufgebaut werden will. Nicht jeder Prozess existiert schon – viele davon gestaltest du selbst. Wenn du für deine Arbeit fertige Strukturen brauchst, ist das wahrscheinlich nicht das Richtige für dich. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team. Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies , We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. We're hiring a German-speaking ADR I to join our Account Development team at Camunda. We're a tight-knit, energetic team that takes outbound seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. We run structured prospecting motions, share what's working in real time, celebrate the wins together, and still allow for flexibility in the way we operate because booking a good meeting takes real work and progressing an opportunity puts ADRs at the forefront of a great GTM motion. This is a strong entry point into tech sales for someone who wants to learn and refine the fundamentals of prospecting, discovery, and pipeline generation inside an enterprise software motion. You'll work directly with Account Executives but will also be responsible for prospecting into your own patch. We ask that all of our ADRs have a remote environment that is conducive to consistent weekly motions and to be able to travel 4-6 times per year, usually a week or less at a time. What you will do: As an ADR I, you'll run long-term outbound and timely inbound prospecting motions to generate qualified pipeline for our sales team. Working emails, sales cadences, social outreach and most importantly calls to get in front of the right people at the right accounts at the right time. This role exists because a sustainable pipeline is built through persistence, consistency, a growth mindset and an ability to diagnose challenges and bring solutions within your own prospecting motion. Generate qualified pipeline by running outbound prospecting across email, phone, event outreach and attendance and LinkedIn into target accounts. Qualify inbound interest through ADR-led scheduled calls and convert into booked meetings for Account Executives. Research accounts, personas and signals to tailor and leverage AI for high touch low impact motions. Partner with Account Executives to understand what constitutes a quality meeting, contact and account, and adjust your approach based on feedback. Exhibit excellent operational hygiene by tracking activity and pipeline health in Salesforce and other sales tools to monitor your own inputs and performance. Learn Camunda's product and value propositions and the process orchestration space well enough to have credible, useful conversations with prospects in specific verticals. What you bring: Fluency in German Some experience with outbound prospecting or customer-facing communication is preferred. This doesn't have to be in sales. Comfort with strict time management and prioritization of requests. You'll be conducting a lot of calls and emails, and you're motivated by the math of it. You will also be given regular enablement and will be responsible for monitoring multiple sources of leads. Curiosity about technology and a willingness to learn a technical product. You take feedback from your manager and AEs seriously and change your approach in a timely and meaningful way based on it. Cross-functional relationships. You have a curiosity as to how things work and which individuals you can support and thus that can support you. You ask questions and challenge the status quo if you’ve experienced a better solution. Ability and/or willingness to use our product . This role is an existing vacancy #LI-JS1 #LI-Remote #DACH What We Have to Offer: Compensation We offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. About the Role:

Hi there! We're hiring a German-speaking ADR I to join our Account Development team at Camunda.

 

We're a tight-knit, energetic team that takes outbound seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. We run structured prospecting motions, share what's working in real time, celebrate the wins together, and still allow for flexibility in the way we operate because booking a good meeting takes real work and progressing an opportunity puts ADRs at the forefront of a great GTM motion.

 

This is a strong entry point into tech sales for someone who wants to learn and refine the fundamentals of prospecting, discovery, and pipeline generation inside an enterprise software motion. You'll work directly with Account Executives but will also be responsible for prospecting into your own patch. We ask that all of our ADRs have a remote environment that is conducive to consistent weekly motions and to be able to travel 4-6 times per year, usually a week or less at a time.

What you will do:

As an ADR I, you'll run long-term outbound and timely inbound prospecting motions to generate qualified pipeline for our sales team. Working emails, sales cadences, social outreach and most importantly calls to get in front of the right people at the right accounts at the right time. This role exists because a sustainable pipeline is built through persistence, consistency, a growth mindset and an ability to diagnose challenges and bring solutions within your own prospecting motion.

  • Generate qualified pipeline by running outbound prospecting across email, phone, event outreach and attendance and LinkedIn into target accounts.

  • Qualify inbound interest through ADR-led scheduled calls and convert into booked meetings for Account Executives.

  • Research accounts, personas and signals to tailor and leverage AI for high touch low impact motions.

  • Partner with Account Executives to understand what constitutes a quality meeting, contact and account, and adjust your approach based on feedback.

  • Exhibit excellent operational hygiene by tracking activity and pipeline health in Salesforce and other sales tools to monitor your own inputs and performance.

  • Learn Camunda's product and value propositions and the process orchestration space well enough to have credible, useful conversations with prospects in specific verticals.

What you bring:

  • Fluency in German

  • Some experience with outbound prospecting or customer-facing communication is preferred. This doesn't have to be in sales. Internships, retail, hospitality, or customer support all count if you know how to build rapport with people, manage expectations and handle rejection.

  • Comfort with strict time management and prioritization of requests. You'll be conducting a lot of calls and emails, and you're motivated by the math of it. You will also be given regular enablement and will be responsible for monitoring multiple sources of leads.

  • Curiosity about technology and a willingness to learn a technical product. You don't need an engineering background, but you need to be genuinely interested in understanding what Camunda does and why it matters to the people you're calling. You share successes.

  • Resilience and self-awareness. You know how to keep going without getting discouraged, and you can tell the difference between a bad day and a bad approach.

  • Coachability. You take feedback from your manager and AEs seriously and change your approach in a timely and meaningful way based on it.

  • Cross-functional relationships. You have a curiosity as to how things work and which individuals you can support and thus that can support you. You ask questions and challenge the status quo if you’ve experienced a better solution.

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product.

About the Role:

Hi there! We're hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager to join our Product Marketing team.

We're a group that cares about getting the story right, not just getting it out the door. We work closely with product, sales, and demand gen, and we hold ourselves to a high bar because our work directly shapes how the market understands what we build.

This role gives you real ownership. You'll shape positioning and messaging for a meaningful piece of our product portfolio, build the competitive intelligence that keeps our field teams sharp, and work directly with sales leaders who depend on your materials to close deals. It's a role with visible impact, not one where your work disappears into a shared drive.

As a Senior Product Marketing Manager, you'll drive go-to-market strategy for your area, from positioning through launch through enablement, while partnering with product and sales to make sure the message actually lands. This role matters because clear, credible product marketing is what turns a strong platform into a business result. Camunda operates in a technical, complex space, and getting that translation right is not optional.

What You Will Do

  • Own positioning and messaging for your product area, translating technical capability into a clear value proposition for both technical and business buyers.

  • Build and maintain a competitive intelligence program that sales actually uses, not just battlecards that sit in a folder.

  • Lead go-to-market execution for launches in your area, coordinating across product, sales, and demand gen so the message is consistent everywhere it shows up.

  • Arm the field with content that works in real conversations: pitch decks, demos, solution briefs, and objection handling.

  • Use market and customer research to inform product and positioning decisions, not just to validate ones already made.

  • Mentor and support other marketers on your team, sharing what you've learned without being asked.

What You Will Bring to the Role

  • Significant experience in B2B product marketing, ideally in enterprise software, with a track record of owning positioning and messaging end to end, not just contributing pieces of it.

  • A real competitive intelligence practice under your belt. You've built and maintained a program that sales relied on, not just responded to research requests as they came in.

  • Comfort marketing technical products to technical buyers. You can go deep enough into a technical concept to be credible with a developer, and simplify it enough to be clear to an executive.

  • Field enablement experience at scale. You've built programs that changed how a sales team talked about a product, and you know how to tell if it worked.

  • Strong cross-functional instincts. You know how to build trust with product and sales without relying on authority, and how to bring people along on a positioning decision rather than just announcing it.

  • Comfort using AI tools in your day to day work. This isn't a checkbox, it's part of how the role actually operates.

title: Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)
description: Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d) Regional Role · Remote, based in the DACH region · Reports to: Sales Director About Everfield Everfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions. We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units. The Opportunity The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region. This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them. Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units. How the Role Operates • Two levels, one standard. The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself. • Direct team leadership where it is needed. Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done. • You are not a seller. You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver. • Reporting. You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams. What You Will Do Sales Execution & Commercial Acceleration • Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth. • Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number. • Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster. • Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation. • Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention. • Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction. • Lead deal/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability. Pipeline Discipline & Forecast Integrity • Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better. • Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews. • Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag. • Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter. Revenue Standards & Definitions • Act as guardian of Everfield's revenue definitions in the region: what counts as a booking, how new name is separated from back to base, how recurring value is recognised, and what enters the pipeline in the first place. • Hold those definitions consistently, including where a Business Unit's own commercial logic pushes against them, and fix the incentive, target, or CRM design underneath rather than bending the measurement. • Make the cluster comparable to every other region, so performance can be read the same way across the portfolio. Commercial Governance • Ensure transparency in quota design, attainment measurement, and sales capacity planning. • Support commission structure alignment with business goals. • Contribute to annual, quarterly, and monthly commercial planning by reality-checking growth assumptions against pipeline health, execution capacity, and historical feasibility. Commercial Diagnostics • Diagnose revenue performance across segments, teams, and funnel stages, identifying where revenue is generated, stalled, or lost. • Produce a written diagnostic and prioritised action plan for each Business Unit you take on, naming the problem, the cause, the cost of inaction, the action, the owner, and the date. • Prioritise your own time across the cluster on distance to target, materiality to the region, and whether a documented plan already exists. • Provide feedback on pricing discipline, discounting practices, packaging effectiveness, and ICP conversion efficiency. • Translate performance signals into executive-level recommendations and commercial action plans. CEO & General Director Partnership • Act as strategic commercial partner to CEOs and Business Unit leaders, representing Everfield's revenue expectations and performance discipline. • Challenge growth assumptions constructively and escalate persistent underperformance when required. What Success Looks Like In the first 12 months: • Full visibility into the commercial funnel, aligned with HQ reporting standards. • Acceleration of organic recurring revenue growth across the region. • Improved reliability of pipeline data and forecast accuracy. • Sales pipelines that more accurately predict bookings performance. • At least one Business Unit where you hold sales management directly and the team delivers against its number. • Reliable visibility of quota attainment and seller productivity. • Deal reviews embedded across portfolio sales teams, resulting in higher win rates and shorter sales cycles. • Revenue per seller increasing steadily across the cluster. • A documented, reusable set of playbooks and diagnostics that other regions can apply without starting again. What We Are Looking For • 6-10 years total experience in B2B SaaS revenue roles, with at least 3-4 years in a sales management position, accountable for a team's bookings performance and not only for personal pipeline contribution. • Track record of consistent revenue target attainment in a management role. You have owned a number and delivered against it, not only improved process quality. • Direct experience leading and developing a sales team, including hiring, coaching, and managing underperformance. raw.title: Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)
raw.description:
Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d)

Regional Role · Remote, based in the DACH region · Reports to: Sales Director

About Everfield

Everfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions.

We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units.

The Opportunity

The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region.

This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them.

Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units.

How the Role Operates

• Two levels, one standard. The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself.

• Direct team leadership where it is needed. Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done.

• You are not a seller. You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver.

• Reporting. You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams.

What You Will Do

Sales Execution & Commercial Acceleration

• Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth.

• Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number.

• Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster.

• Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation.

• Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention.

• Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction.

• Lead deal/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability.

Pipeline Discipline & Forecast Integrity

• Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better.

• Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews.

• Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag.

• Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter.

Revenue Standards & Definitions

• Act as guardian of Everfield's revenue definitions in the region: what counts as a booking, how new name is separated from back to base, how recurring value is recognised, and what enters the pipeline in the first place.

• Hold those definitions consistently, including where a Business Unit's own commercial logic pushes against them, and fix the incentive, target, or CRM design underneath rather than bending the measurement.

• Make the cluster comparable to every other region, so performance can be read the same way across the portfolio.

Commercial Governance

• Ensure transparency in quota design, attainment measurement, and sales capacity planning.

• Support commission structure alignment with business goals.

• Contribute to annual, quarterly, and monthly commercial planning by reality-checking growth assumptions against pipeline health, execution capacity, and historical feasibility.

Commercial Diagnostics

• Diagnose revenue performance across segments, teams, and funnel stages, identifying where revenue is generated, stalled, or lost.

• Produce a written diagnostic and prioritised action plan for each Business Unit you take on, naming the problem, the cause, the cost of inaction, the action, the owner, and the date.

• Prioritise your own time across the cluster on distance to target, materiality to the region, and whether a documented plan already exists.

• Provide feedback on pricing discipline, discounting practices, packaging effectiveness, and ICP conversion efficiency.

• Translate performance signals into executive-level recommendations and commercial action plans.

CEO & General Director Partnership

• Act as strategic commercial partner to CEOs and Business Unit leaders, representing Everfield's revenue expectations and performance discipline.

• Challenge growth assumptions constructively and escalate persistent underperformance when required.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 12 months:

• Full visibility into the commercial funnel, aligned with HQ reporting standards.

• Acceleration of organic recurring revenue growth across the region.

• Improved reliability of pipeline data and forecast accuracy.

• Sales pipelines that more accurately predict bookings performance.

• At least one Business Unit where you hold sales management directly and the team delivers against its number.

• Reliable visibility of quota attainment and seller productivity.

• Deal reviews embedded across portfolio sales teams, resulting in higher win rates and shorter sales cycles.

• Revenue per seller increasing steadily across the cluster.

• A documented, reusable set of playbooks and diagnostics that other regions can apply without starting again.

What We Are Looking For

• 6-10 years total experience in B2B SaaS revenue roles, with at least 3-4 years in a sales management position, accountable for a team's bookings performance and not only for personal pipeline contribution.

• Track record of consistent revenue target attainment in a management role. You have owned a number and delivered against it, not only improved process quality.

• Direct experience leading and developing a sales team, including hiring, coaching, and managing underperformance. You will do this again here, inside our Business Units.

• Track record of implementing structured pipeline management: defining stage criteria, enforcing qualification standards, running deal reviews, and improving forecast reliability.

• Experience diagnosing revenue performance across the full funnel: understanding where deals are lost, why cycles extend, and what structural issues limit growth.

• Manages through CRM data: uses pipeline data to run structured deal reviews, identify risk, and hold sellers accountable to data quality. Familiar with Salesforce or HubSpot as a management tool.

• Experience working with senior stakeholders (CEOs, founders, or general managers) on commercial performance, including navigating organisational resistance and earning trust before driving change.

• Experience adapting sales management approach across companies at different sales maturity levels: able to calibrate coaching, process rigour, and expectations to fit the context.

• German fluency required, with professional English for work across the group. European B2B SaaS market experience required.

• Commercial finance literacy is a strong advantage: reading a P&L, understanding revenue recognition, and being able to argue the return on a commercial investment.

• Private-equity-backed or multi-entity SaaS environment experience is a strong advantage.

Skills

• Structured coaching and seller development: designing and running structured 1:1s, deal reviews, and field accompaniment to build individual seller capability, not just inspect opportunities.

• Pipeline discipline and forecasting: reading a pipeline critically, identifying risk early, and improving forecast reliability.

• Change management: driving commercial process adoption across multiple teams, and building momentum without relying on formal authority.

• Documentation and knowledge scale: writing down what you diagnose and what you implement, in a form another person can pick up and run. Work that lives only in conversation does not scale across a portfolio, and anything you build for one Business Unit should be reusable in the next.

• Commercial planning and challenge: building a bottom-up view of what revenue targets are achievable, pressure-testing top-down assumptions, and presenting credible alternatives to leadership.

• Commercial storytelling: presenting clear, honest risk assessments to CEOs and senior leadership, and leading a review that drives decisions rather than just restating numbers.

  • Full Business proficiency in German and English is a must

Who You Are

• You lead teams and you influence without authority. You will manage sellers directly in some Business Units and hold no formal authority in others. Both need to work. You build trust quickly and drive change through credibility, clarity, and structured analysis.

• You are hands-on with sales execution. You are comfortable stepping into real deals, reviewing opportunities with sellers, and diagnosing pipeline issues directly with the team, without needing to be the person closing.

• You combine analytical thinking with practical commercial judgement. You interpret pipeline data, and you also understand the realities of getting deals done.

• You communicate clearly and directly. You raise commercial risks early, with a recommendation attached, and challenge assumptions constructively, including when performance doesn't meet expectations.

You are pragmatic in complex environments. Portfolio companies vary in maturity and commercial model. You bring discipline without imposing rigid process that doesn't fit the situation

Group Director interview

title: Member of Technical Staff - Safety
description: About Black Forest Labs We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX—foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and video. We're creating the generative models that power how people make images and video—tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started. Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity. Why this role FLUX models ship as open weights, which gives anyone full access to the model. Our safety efforts focus on suppressing harmful behaviors and mitigating the risk of misuse, so safety has to be built into the models themselves, not bolted on afterwards. As a Member of Technical Staff on our safety research team, you'll research and ship methods that make FLUX models safe by design: from what goes into the training data to how the models are mid- and post-trained, across images, video and the text that conditions them. This is a role with real ownership: you won't just do research on model safety, you'll shape it. The methods you build ship in FLUX models with over 75 million downloads on Hugging Face and in production at some of the largest platforms in the world. What you'll work on Develop mid- and post-training safety methods for FLUX models, such as safety SFT, preference optimization and RL with safety rewards, and concept erasure. Build safety data filtering that runs at pretraining scale: classifiers and pipelines that screen billions of images, video clips and captions, with measured Pareto frontiers and precision/recall trade-offs. Make safety hold up for open-weight releases, including robustness to adversarial prompts and to downstream fine-tuning. Extend safety to the text side of the stack: prompts, captions and the text encoders that condition our models. Design evaluations and red-teaming that measure harmful generations alongside image quality and prompt following, so safety gains don't come at the cost of performance. Work directly with pretraining and post-training teams so your methods land in the release model, and publish where it makes sense. What we're looking for Hands-on research experience in visual safety: safety of text-to-image, text-to-video or vision-language models, such as harm classifiers, safe generation methods or safety benchmarks. Proven experience in at least one of: Large-scale safety data filtering: building and running classifiers or filtering pipelines over hundreds of millions of samples or more. Safety mid- or post-training: safety SFT, DPO or RL with safety objectives, or unlearning applied to large generative models. Deep familiarity with concept erasure methods (e.g. ESD, UCE, adversarial unlearning) and their failure modes, such as concept recovery and collateral damage to unrelated concepts. Track record of shipping: top-venue publications (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV) paired with production impact, or unambiguous production wins at a frontier lab. Experience with distributed training at multi-node scale. Strong PyTorch fluency; you write research code that others can build on. You work fluently with coding agents to move faster, and have the depth to verify their output and own the result. Experience running multi-agent workflows: you know which tasks to hand off and which to keep yourself, and you use the speed-up to raise the quality bar, not lower it. We'd be especially excited if you: Know how to keep safety intact after release, when others fine-tune open weights. Have tackled safety for video generation, where harm can emerge across frames rather than in any single frame. Bring experience with audio safety, especially for jointly generated audio and video, where each modality can amplify harm in the other. Have unlearned concepts from text encoders or built safety-tuned encoders (e.g. Safe-CLIP-style approaches). Have worked on text safety: LLM safety tuning, prompt and jailbreak defenses, or text safety classifiers, ideally across languages. Have applied latent-space safety methods, such as activation steering or safe guidance. Have built VLM-based safety judges or guard models for filtering or evaluation. How we work together We're a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. You'll join us in Freiburg at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week). We'll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we've structured things to make it accessible to all. We'll discuss what this will look like for the role during our interview process. Everything we do is grounded in four values: Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful. Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task. Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect. Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.   • Work directly with pretraining and post-training teams so your methods land in the release model, and publish where it makes sense.

What we're looking for

  • Hands-on research experience in visual safety: safety of text-to-image, text-to-video or vision-language models, such as harm classifiers, safe generation methods or safety benchmarks.

  • Proven experience in at least one of:

    • Large-scale safety data filtering: building and running classifiers or filtering pipelines over hundreds of millions of samples or more.

    • Safety mid- or post-training: safety SFT, DPO or RL with safety objectives, or unlearning applied to large generative models.

  • Experience with distributed training at multi-node scale.

title: Robotics Application Engineer
description: At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality. Robotics Application Engineer – Rhoda AI GmbH (Germany) About Rhoda AI GmbH Rhoda AI GmbH is Rhoda AI's first international entity, established to own strategic partner relationships across Europe and drive deployment of Robotics as a Service (RaaS). It's a small, high-ownership team: you'll work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one, with a direct line to our engineering organization in Silicon Valley. About the Application Engineering Team Application Engineering is where Rhoda's AI meets the real world. We work directly with customers and strategic partners to understand their operational problems, determine where our platform can deliver value, and lead the application of Rhoda's AI model end to end — from model post-training and data collection, to robot tooling and work-cell design, to production deployments on the customer's floor. The team sits at the intersection of engineering, product, deployment operations, and business, with members in the US and Germany. Application Engineering is organized into three complementary roles — Application Engineers, Solution Engineers, and Technical Program Managers. The Role As a Robotics Application Engineer, you are a core member of Rhoda AI's European team and the hands-on technical lead in the early stages of a partner engagement — Scoping, Proof of Principle (POP), and Proof of Concept (POC) — through to RaaS deployment. You'll determine whether a use case is feasible, design and prototype the end effectors and task tooling a robot needs to do the job, write the data collection procedures that feed our models, and post-train Rhoda's AI model to perform the task. You'll spend real time on partner sites across Europe standing up POCs and showing what our platform can do. You'll also serve as a key technical bridge between our European partners and Rhoda HQ Engineering, owning the feedback loop that turns field findings into product improvements. What You'll Do Scope new partner use cases alongside the commercial team: ask the right questions, assess technical feasibility, and make go/no-go recommendations. Design, prototype, and iterate on end effectors and task-specific tooling for real-world manipulation tasks. Author and refine data collection SOPs, and work with teleoperation and ML ops teams to gather high-quality training data. Post-train and evaluate Rhoda's AI model on partner tasks, driving performance toward POC success criteria. Lead on-site POP/POC setup and execution, including model training, daily reporting, validation, and direct partner interaction, and author the final technical report. Partner with Solution Engineers on task engineering and solution design input as engagements move toward production. Review proposals and provide technical feedback ahead of purchase orders. Support model training through Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), deployment, and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT). Lead root cause analysis for issues surfaced during deployments, troubleshooting across hardware, firmware, and software until the real cause is found. Share field learnings with product and engineering in Silicon Valley, translating partner-reported issues into prioritized, actionable input for the roadmap. Present clear, non-technical summaries of technical outcomes to partner leadership, and work with the commercial team to tie them to commercial milestones. What You'll Bring BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field. 3–8 years of hands-on experience in robotics, automation, systems integration, or applied engineering in an industrial setting, including real-world deployments or field installations. Strong mechanical design skills, including CAD (e.g., SolidWorks, Onshape, Fusion) and rapid prototyping (3D printing, machining, off-the-shelf components). Working knowledge of machine learning workflows — data collection, training, and evaluation — and comfort working in Python. Experience with robot arms, grippers, and sensors (cameras, depth sensors, LiDAR, IMUs) in real environments, including integration and calibration. Proven track record conducting root cause analysis on complex systems spanning hardware, firmware, and software. Strong problem-solving skills and comfort working with ambiguity in high-stakes environments. Clear communicator who can explain technical tradeoffs to partners, executives, and internal teams. Fluent English required; German at working level minimum. Willingness to travel approximately 40% across Europe, including extended on-site POC periods, with occasional travel to the US. Nice to Have Experience with imitation learning, VLA models, world models, or robot foundation models. Background in factory automation, material handling, or logistics. Experience in a customer-facing technical role (application, field, FDE, or sales engineering) at a robotics OEM, system integrator, or corporate automation department. Familiarity with teleoperation systems or remote robot management workflows. Experience with ROS/ROS2, embedded Linux, or C/Rust for onboard software. Why Rhoda AI GmbH Work on real customer problems, not lab demos: our robots are ready for field deployment directly after a successful POC. Direct line to HQ Engineering — your field intelligence shapes the product roadmap. Small, high-ownership team where you work with the Managing Director and Commercial Lead as peers from day one.   • Debug fabric problems wherever they show up, from a flapping link to a job that’s mysteriously slow

  • Evaluate and select AI Fabric vendors and hardware, and push back with data when something doesn’t meet spec

title: Sales Excellence Manager
description: As a Sales Excellence Manager (m/w/d), you will find where our sales funnel leaks and where we engage customers too slowly, then work with the sales teams until it is fixed across our global markets. You will own revenue per worked hour as our core productivity KPI, run capacity planning and bonus governance, and set the build priorities that turn your findings into tools. Analysis is your starting point, not your deliverable: you are measured on whether conversion, speed to lead and productivity actually move in each market. PERGOLUX designs and sells premium, Scandinavian-inspired outdoor living products, from aluminium pergolas to garden furniture, directly to consumers. You'll need enough craft depth to recognise excellent work, challenge it constructively, and help designers get better. The team needs a manager whose design judgment they trust. You'll manage a team spanning product designers, design engineers and user researchers at a range of seniority levels, working across our product areas. You'll work alongside our other design manager. You'll report to our VP of Product until our Head of Design joins the team. That search is running now. More than 80% of workflows built on n8n involve AI agents, and we're widening from a developer audience to a broader set of builders. That shift is the central design problem here, and your team is at the centre of it. 🎯 Your main goal is to build a Product Design team that consistently produces excellent work and shapes how n8n's product evolves. Here's what that involves: Lead and develop the team Run regular, high-quality 1:1s and coach designers, design engineers and researchers across different levels. Own performance management: evidence-based reviews, honest feedback, and real support for anyone who isn't where they need to be. Help people understand what's expected at their level and what growth looks like, evolving our progression framework for Product Design. Hire excellent designers as the team grows, and broaden the range of backgrounds and perspectives on the team. Raise the design bar Set and hold a high standard across problem framing, user understanding, interaction design, information architecture and visual craft. raw.title: Product Design Manager
raw.description:
The AI orchestration of your wildest imagination.

n8n is the open workflow orchestration platform built for the new era of AI. We give technical teams the freedom of code with the speed of no-code, so they can automate faster, smarter, and without limits. Backed by a fiercely inventive community and 500+ builder-approved integrations, we’re changing the way people bring systems together and scale ideas for impact.

Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve:

  • Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders

  • Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects

  • Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation


That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register.

We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.

We're looking for an experienced design manager to lead our Product Design team.

This is a management role. Your job is to develop designers, raise the quality of the work, and make sure design has real influence on where the product goes. It is not a player-coach role, and it is not a step up for a strong IC looking for their first management position. We need someone who has already managed product designers and can do it well from day one.

n8n is a powerful, flexible technical tool, which means the problems your team tackles are complex. Design decisions have to account for diverse user workflows, technical constraints, and how changes ripple across the whole platform. You'll need enough craft depth to recognise excellent work, challenge it constructively, and help designers get better. The team needs a manager whose design judgment they trust.

You'll manage a team spanning product designers, design engineers and user researchers at a range of seniority levels, working across our product areas. You'll work alongside our other design manager. You'll report to our VP of Product until our Head of Design joins the team. That search is running now.

More than 80% of workflows built on n8n involve AI agents, and we're widening from a developer audience to a broader set of builders. That shift is the central design problem here, and your team is at the centre of it.

🎯 Your main goal is to build a Product Design team that consistently produces excellent work and shapes how n8n's product evolves. Here's what that involves:


Lead and develop the team

  • Run regular, high-quality 1:1s and coach designers, design engineers and researchers across different levels.

  • Own performance management: evidence-based reviews, honest feedback, and real support for anyone who isn't where they need to be.

  • Help people understand what's expected at their level and what growth looks like, evolving our progression framework for Product Design.

  • Hire excellent designers as the team grows, and broaden the range of backgrounds and perspectives on the team.

Raise the design bar

  • Set and hold a high standard across problem framing, user understanding, interaction design, information architecture and visual craft.

  • Facilitate design critiques and reviews that measurably improve the work, and help designers think beyond the feature in front of them.

  • Develop designers' judgment and autonomy rather than becoming the final approval layer for every decision.

Own the whole product experience

  • Keep a holistic view across features and product areas, identifying inconsistencies, recurring UX problems, and opportunities for more coherent patterns.

  • Work with the team to address fragmentation systematically rather than feature by feature.

Make design a real partner

  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering leadership so design contributes early to problem definition and product direction, not late to execution.

  • Help designers influence product decisions through strong reasoning rather than positional authority.

  • Improve how the team works across critique, collaboration, decision-making and knowledge sharing, introducing structure where it helps the team scale and resisting process that slows things down.

How much of this is hands-on?

Worth being direct, because it's the question every good candidate asks. This is a management role: developing designers, raising the bar, and making design count in product decisions is the job, and that's where your time goes.

You'll stay close to the craft in critiques, in reviews and in the detail of the work, and you'll occasionally pick up design work yourself. When that happens it sits outside the squads and varies with the period: an exploratory concept, a gap during someone's leave, a problem that needs a first pass. It is not a 50/50 split, and if what you want is to keep a squad's worth of delivery alongside managing the team, this isn't the role.

REQUIREMENTS

Must-haves

  • 👥 Proven design management: You've managed product designers in a product-led technology company for 3+ years, with a team of five or more. This is not a first management role.

  • 🧭 Running a team well: You've run effective 1:1s, evidence-based performance reviews and difficult feedback conversations, including with people who weren't performing. You've built or improved a career progression framework for designers, and you're comfortable with the administrative side of managing a team rather than treating it as overhead.

  • 📈 Growing people: You coach and mentor, you run critique that changes the work, and you can point to specific designers who got measurably better or grew in scope while reporting to you.

  • 🎨 Design taste and judgment: Your own craft is strong enough that designers trust your read on quality, you can articulate what separates adequate design from excellent design, and you'll step into the work directly when the situation calls for it.

  • 🎯 Hiring: You've hired designers consistently well, you know where good design talent is and how to attract it, and you can tell the difference quickly.

  • 🤖 AI fluency: You use AI tools hands-on in your own work and in how your team designs, and you have an informed view on designing AI-enabled products. AI agents are the product here, so this one is not optional.

Nice-to-haves

  • 🛠️ Technical products: You've managed design teams in B2B SaaS, developer tools, workflow automation or similarly technical products.

  • 🧠 Technical mindset: You don't need to write code, but genuine curiosity about what's happening underneath (APIs, webhooks, data structures, how workflows actually execute) earns you credibility with engineers here.

  • 👩‍💻 Designing for developers: You've designed products for developers, technical operators or other sophisticated users.

  • 🔭 Systems view: You can step back from individual projects to spot patterns and UX problems across a broader product experience.

  • 🤝 Influence without authority: You bring Product and Engineering peers with you through reasoning rather than positional authority.

  • 📊 Scaling teams: You've grown a design team through a period of rapid company growth.

  • 🌍 Distributed teams: You've managed designers in remote-first or highly distributed organisations.

  • 🔓 Open source: You've worked on open-source or community-driven products.

  • 🌱 Inclusive hiring: You've meaningfully broadened the diversity of a design team through how you hire.

Our hiring process

We'll tell you the whole shape of it upfront, and there's very little homework.

  1. Screening call with our recruiter. 45 minutes, no prep.

  2. Leading designers with the hiring manager, 75 minutes. You'll present for 20 minutes on a team you built, grew or turned around. Reuse existing material; it shouldn't take more than two or three hours. We don't need case studies of your own design work.

  3. Live critique and coaching, 60 minutes. We'll send you a real piece of n8n design work 24 hours ahead. You'll critique it, then have a coaching conversation with the designer who made it. No preparation beyond reading it and trying the product.

  4. Conversation with our VP of Product, and a culture call with Jan, our CEO. 45 minutes each, same day where we can.

  5. Meet two or three of the designers you'd be managing. Not scored; it's for you as much as for us.

We'll also ask for two references, one of them a former direct report. A portfolio is welcome if you have one, though we know not every design manager keeps theirs current.

Why join us?

At n8n, your work won't disappear into a slide deck. You'll lead design for a product that hundreds of thousands of builders use to automate real work, sitting right where developer tools, AI agents and no-code interaction models meet. The design problems are genuinely hard and largely unsolved.

You're inheriting an established team with strong designers, not building from zero, and there's real room to shape how the team coaches, critiques, grows and works with Product and Engineering, rather than inheriting a rigid design organisation. You'll stay close enough to the craft to influence quality directly, while your main job is making the designers around you better.

You'll join a fast-growing, Europe remote-first company where autonomy, experimentation, and craft matter, at the point where n8n is scaling from a beloved open-source project into a major B2B platform. Design's contribution to product thinking is established here, and has a long way still to run.

Sound like a challenge you're excited to take on?

Apply now and help us build the future of automation.

n8n is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We can sponsor visas to Germany; for any other country, you need to have existing right to work.

Our company language is English.

You care about diversity and inclusion? We do too! Check out our Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging initiatives at n8n (https://www.notion.so/n8n/Diversity-inclusion-and-belonging-n8n-c1bec2fff536422d868b1a438d990e35).

Location disclaimer: If you see multiple job postings for the same role, it is most likely because we're hiring remotely for this role and posting in different locations to make sure every potential candidate can see the role. Please apply to the location you're the most likely to work from in the future.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation 💸 – We offer fair and attractive pay.

  • Ownership 💪 – Our core value is to “empower others,” and we mean it—you’ll get a slice of n8n with equity.

  • Work/life balance 🏖️ – We work hard but ensure you have time to recharge:

    • Europe: 30 days of vacation, plus public holidays wherever you are.

    • US: 20 vacation days, 8 sick days, plus public holidays wherever you are.

  • Health & wellness 🩺 –

    • Europe: We provide benefits according to local country norms.*

    • US: Multiple low-premium, low-deductible medical plans with coverage for individuals and families—plus a no-cost premium HDHP option with a pre-seeded HSA—along with dental and vision coverage.

  • Future planning 💰 –

    • Europe: We provide pension contributions according to local country norms.*

    • US: 401(k) retirement plan with a 4% employer match.

  • Financial security 🛡️ –

    • Europe: We provide benefits according to local country norms.*

    • US: Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance, plus life insurance to support you and your loved ones.

  • Career growth 📈 – We hire rising stars who grow with us! You’ll get €1K (or equivalent) per year to spend on courses, books, events, or coaching to level up your skills.

  • A passionate team 🤩 – We love our product, and we prove it with regular hackathons where we see who can build the coolest thing with it!

  • Remote-first 🌏 – Our team works remotely across Europe, with regular off-sites for team bonding. Some roles, like sales in the US, are hybrid—please check the job description.

  • Giving back 🤝 – We're big fans of open source, and you'll get $100 per month to support projects you care about.

  • Transparency 🙏 – We all know what everyone’s working on, how the company is doing—the whole shebang.

*Country and/or State specific details provided in your employment agreement.

title: Senior AI Content Producer - Foto, Video, Motion (m/w/d)
description: Bei Rosental Organics bist du kein klassischer Fotograf oder Videograf – du bist der Content Multiplier. Ein Shoot wird bei dir zu 50+ Assets, ein UGC-Clip zu 30 Hook-Variants, ein Produktfoto zu 20 Format-Adaptionen. Der Meta-Algorithmus belohnt Volumen und Diversität, und genau das lieferst du: aus einer Kampagne wird bei dir ein ganzer Wochen-Feed für Paid Social. Du produzierst und multiplizierst Foto-, Video- und Motion-Content für Paid Ads, Social, CRM und E-Commerce, mit klarem Fokus auf Performance und Testing-Volumen. Du drehst und shootest schnell und hands-on mit modernem Setup: UGC, Product, Lifestyle, Studio – End-to-End und ohne Assistenz-Kette. Einen skalierbaren AI-Workflow baust du selbst auf, der Rohmaterial in Dutzende testbare Variants verwandelt: Hook-Iterations, Cutdowns, Format-Adaptions, Kontext-Wechsel, Voiceover-Varianten, Motion-Loops. Du entwickelst High-Performing Creatives für Meta, TikTok und CRM mit Fokus auf Hook Rate, Watchtime, CTR und ROAS. Mindestens 3 neue AI-Tools pro Jahr integrierst du produktiv in unseren Stack (Runway, Nano Banana, Kive, ElevenLabs, Topaz, CapCut AI, Descript – was heute liefert, ersetzt du morgen). Performance-Dashboards liest du selbst, ziehst die Insights und übersetzt sie am gleichen Tag in neue Variants und Hypothesen. Du bringst 3+ Jahre Erfahrung in Content Production für D2C/ E-Commerce, Performance Marketing oder ein hochdynamisches Growth-Umfeld mit, inklusive starker Paid-Social-Cases (Meta, TikTok). Dein Portfolio zeigt echte Performance-Ergebnisse (Hook Rate, Watchtime, CTR, ROAS) und Beispiele, wie du aus einem Asset viele gemacht hast, keine Editorial-Reels, keine Behance-Moodboards. Neue AI-Tools lernst du eigenständig und schnell: Runway, Nano Banana, Kive, ElevenLabs, CapCut AI, Descript und Topaz sind dir vertraut, und den nächsten Tool-Sprung hast du meist schon selbst identifiziert. Du drehst, shootest und schneidest selbst (≥ 85 %): Sony/Canon, Studio-Light und Natural-Light, Premiere Pro, CapCut, Photoshop und Lightroom auf sehr hohem Niveau, mit Meta-Funnel-Logik im Schlaf (Hooks Sek. 1, Pattern Interrupt, Pacing). Aus einem Shot 50 Assets zu machen, klingt für dich nach Chance statt Qualitätsverlust; Premium-Ästhetik ohne Kompromisse ist für dich selbstverständlich, AI-Output darf nie nach AI-Output aussehen. Du liest Zahlen und übersetzt sie direkt in Creative-Entscheidungen, strukturiert, direkt, belastbar. Deutsch mind. C1. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Das Gesicht unserer Brand auf TikTok
description: Manche Dinge muss man nicht erklären. TRIONE ist eine Luxury Lifestyle Brand für Accessoires und Schmuck, designed in Marbella. Japanische Seidenkordel, graviertes Gold, Details, die man erst auf den zweiten Blick entdeckt und dann nicht mehr vergisst. Unser ONE Armband ist kein Accessoire, es ist ein Statement für Menschen, die nicht laut sein müssen, um gesehen zu werden. Jetzt bringen wir TRIONE auf TikTok. Nicht mit Countdowns und Rabattcodes, sondern mit Ästhetik, Haltung und Geschichten. Mit Videos und ausgewählten Livestreams aus unserem eigenen Store, von unseren Events und von Orten, die so besonders sind wie unsere Pieces. Dafür suchen wir die Person, die unsere Welt vor der Kamera spürbar macht. Deine Rolle Du bist das Gesicht von TRIONE auf TikTok, in Videos und in Livestreams aus unserem Store, von exklusiven Events und luxuriösen Locations Du erzählst die Geschichten hinter unseren Pieces, nicht ihre Preise Du gestaltest mit uns Content, der sich anfühlt wie die Brand selbst: ruhig, ästhetisch, selbstbewusst Du bist dabei, wenn eine Brand ihre nächste Ebene erreicht Was dich ausmacht Natürliche Präsenz vor der Kamera Ein Auge für Ästhetik, Fashion und Details Du verstehst TikTok und weißt, was Menschen wirklich innehalten lässt Stil, Verlässlichkeit und sehr gutes Deutsch Was dich erwartet Sichtbarkeit als Gesicht einer Brand, die man nicht übersieht Einladungen zu unseren exklusiven Events und Zugang zu unserem Netzwerk aus Creatorn und Partnern Pieces aus unserer Kollektion Ein kleines Team, kurze Wege und echter Einfluss auf das, was entsteht Flexible Zeiten neben Uni oder Job Für wen Diese Stelle ist als Pflichtpraktikum ausgeschrieben und richtet sich an Studierende, die laut Studien- oder Prüfungsordnung ihrer Hochschule ein Pflichtpraktikum absolvieren müssen. Da es sich um ein gesetzlich geregeltes Pflichtpraktikum handelt, ist keine Vergütung vorgesehen. Dafür bekommst du Pieces aus unserer Kollektion, Zugang zu unseren Events und eine Praktikumsbescheinigung für deine Hochschule. Start ist ab sofort. Online Marketing Manager (m/w/d) - Vollzeit | München | Festanstellung

Im Auftrag unseres Partnerunternehmens in München suchen wir Sie zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt als „Online Marketing Manager (m/w/d)“.

Aufgaben

  • Als Performance Marketing Manager (m/w/d) verantworten Sie das gesamte Inhouse-Performance-Marketing einschließlich der strategischen Planung und operativen Umsetzung
  • Zudem entwickeln und optimieren Sie Kampagnen auf Kanälen wie Google Ads, Meta, Display und Affiliate und steuern die entsprechenden Marketingbudgets
  • Darüber hinaus planen und koordinieren Sie saisonale Marketingaktionen, Verkaufsaktionen und Produktlaunches in enger Abstimmung mit den Grafik- und Content-Teams
  • Zusätzlich betreuen und optimieren Sie das Tracking- und Feedmanagement einschließlich Tracking-Links, Pixeln und Produktfeeds
  • Dabei analysieren Sie relevante Performance-Kennzahlen, erstellen regelmäßige Reportings und leiten gezielte Optimierungsmaßnahmen ab

Qualifikation

  • Sie verfügen über ein abgeschlossenes Studium in Marketing, Betriebswirtschaftslehre oder E-Commerce oder eine vergleichbare Ausbildung
  • Sie bringen mehrjährige Berufserfahrung als Performance Marketing Manager (m/w/d), Online Marketing Manager (m/w/d) oder Digital Marketing Manager (m/w/d) mit
  • Sie besitzen fundierte Kenntnisse im Kampagnenmanagement, in der Budgetsteuerung und in der Analyse relevanter Marketing-KPIs
  • Zusätzlich verfügen Sie über Erfahrung mit Performance-Marketing-Kanälen wie Google Ads und Meta sowie fließende Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse
  • Wichtig sind analytisches Denken, Kommunikationsstärke, Teamfähigkeit und eine ausgeprägte Hands-on-Mentalität

Benefits

  • Work-Life-Balance: Freuen Sie sich auf flexible Arbeitszeiten im Gleitzeitmodell
  • Sicherheit: Unbefristete Jobmöglichkeit im Rahmen der Direktvermittlung
  • Gesundheit: Ergonomische Arbeitsplätze sowie zahlreiche Sport- und Gesundheitsangebote sorgen dafür, dass Sie sich rundum wohlfühlen
  • Entwicklung: Auf Sie warten zahlreiche Weiterbildungs- und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten
  • Vielseitigkeit: Freuen Sie sich aufspannende und abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeiten in einem dynamischen Umfeld

title: Lead Systems Engineer (Orbital Launch)
description: Lead Systems Engineer We are looking for a Lead Systems Engineer to act as the Systems Technical Authority for our orbital rocket programme. You will lead the vehicle-level systems effort, maintaining a coherent technical view of the complete vehicle and leading the definition, management, and resolution of system interfaces. Working with multidisciplinary teams across avionics, software, structures, propulsion, GNC, and more, you will manage the interdependencies between technical departments and use model-based systems engineering (MBSE) to keep system-level decisions connected. Your work will lay the technical foundation for successful vehicle integration and launch. About us We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications. We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket. We are working hard to build something truly spectacular. To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you. At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Act as the Systems Technical Authority for the orbital rocket programme, providing vehicle-level systems leadership and maintaining technical coherence across the complete vehicle. Lead the definition, ownership, and resolution of system interfaces across avionics, software, structures, propulsion, GNC, and other technical departments. Identify and manage interdependencies, assumptions, constraints, and cross-subsystem impacts as the vehicle design develops. Use MBSE models and related system artefacts to maintain a connected view of vehicle architecture, requirements, and interfaces. Lead cross-disciplinary systems discussions and reviews, bringing forward system-level trade-offs, resolving technical conflicts, and ensuring decisions are clearly recorded. Coordinate technical departments around vehicle-level priorities and help keep subsystem work aligned with the needs of the overall programme. Track system-level issues and interface actions through to resolution, helping establish the conditions for successful vehicle integration and launch. What we’re looking for Strong understanding of model-based systems engineering and its application to complex, multidisciplinary engineering programmes. Strong understanding of rocketry and how vehicle subsystems interact across the complete system. Experience leading systems engineering work, system interfaces, or cross-disciplinary technical efforts on complex engineering projects. A proven track record of successfully completing engineering projects. The ability to maintain a vehicle-level perspective while engaging with technical teams across avionics, software, structures, propulsion, GNC, and other disciplines. Confidence facilitating technical decisions, managing competing subsystem needs, and driving interface issues toward resolution. About us

We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications.

We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket.
