To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you.

At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the definition, ownership, and resolution of system interfaces across avionics, software, structures, propulsion, GNC, and other technical departments.

title: Engineering Intern
description: About Atira Atira builds the commercial brain for industrials. Our agents 10x the sales engineers of today by offering the complete toolbox of tasks needed in complex environments. They handle everything from extracting and classifying requirements from incoming RFQs, orchestrating communication and information retrieval across multiple stakeholders and systems, while generating outcomes like documentation, production system inputs, or configuration recommendations. CRM. Atira. ERP. We are one of the fastest growing teams in Munich and are looking for you to join us! Why engineers are the foundation of everything Atira ships As an Engineering Intern at Atira, you will work on frontier AI technology, such as (recursive) agent harnesses, runtimes, evals, inference and self-verification in complex engineering domains. You build the frameworks, primitives and scaffolding that let agents reliably handle complex industrial processes end to end, from the first inbound RFQ to the write-back into ERP. Misreading or wrongly interpreting a spec can cost a manufacturer six figures, so the challenges are real and the margin for error is thin. Where you trained matters less than what you've built and how clearly you can describe what broke. Atira is at a stage where you must own problems end to end, because what you ship today is what our customers use tomorrow. What you will do Work on the agent runtime and harnesses. You improve the core components that let Atira's agents reason in complex engineering environments across the entire sales-engineering lifecycle, orchestrate themselves recursively at scale through dynamic programs, and handle arbitrarily large amounts of data. This includes the runtime/sandboxing, the harness, and the outer orchestration layer that ties it together Build out our AI moat. You are in charge of improving quality & evals, improving the ontology layer that unlocks compounding process knowledge and fusing deterministic guardrails with agentic agency to make our agents actionable at enterprise level complexity Unlock industrial scale. Industrials live in multi-modal, data-heavy environments: 1000-page inbounds, pricing lists, CAD files, ERP tables, legacy applications. You scale the AI systems behind them to millions of concurrent LLM requests in isolated sandboxes, with no silent failures, cost blowouts or latency explosions. Advance our internal tooling. FDEs, platform engineers and the GTM team depend on tooling you build to improve Atira's internal context layer, ambient agents, insight and observability engines Work with FDEs when customer problems hit the platform. When an FDE hits a problem they should be able to pull you in. At a team of 20, the boundary between AI, platform and customer is thin, and you'll cross it regularly What we are looking for Ownership, depth, and the instinct to take problems personally, go deep until you understand the system, and own the outcome including the parts that broke. Your profile Agent fluency sits on top of real engineering fundamentals. Solid skills in Python, TypeScript, or a comparable language. We value someone that can still code without AI. Ideally paired with hands-on experience with agents, evals, harnesses, runtimes, sandboxing and tools You've gone further than most with AI-assisted development. Whether it's Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or your own setup, you've invested seriously in building the skills, context, and workflows to get maximum leverage from coding agents. This isn't a nice-to-have. We think engineers who have mastered this are fundamentally more productive, and we hire accordingly You reason clearly about technical tradeoffs. You don’t need to have run systems at scale yet, but you can think through how a design would hold up at thousands of requests per second and explain the pros and cons of different approaches. Every design has tradeoffs: no free lunch You’ve demonstrated ownership and initiative. A side project you took further than anyone asked, a serious open-source contribution, a research project or a startup. We want evidence that you build without being told to and can explain what broke and why You have a strong technical foundation. Enrolled or recently graduated in Computer Science, Information Systems, AI, or a related technical field from a strong technical university (cracked dropouts can qualify too though) Full working proficiency in English. German is not required You're ready for a real internship, not a side gig. You can commit to at least three months full-time, on-site in Munich What you'll get Real ownership: you'll be one of the early team members and shape both product and architecture as well as work closely with customers Strong peers and mentorship: work with and learn from engineers who have shipped AI systems in industrial environments at scale, with the opportunity for mentorship along the way Impactful work: your code is deployed all across Europe’s and US industrial backbone, affecting how complex products and services are sold and configured worldwide Competitive salary and additional benefits Most importantly: Collaborate & thrive in a high-performing but caring culture. We will own the industrial sales function but will do so with modesty and integrity What success looks like at the end of the internship You've shipped meaningful improvements to the agent runtime, our AI pipelines and related systems that are running in production across multiple customer deployments You own one well-defined piece of our AI stack end to end (an eval suite, an internal tool, part of the context layer or the SDK), and the team trusts your judgment on how it should evolve When something breaks in the part you own, you can trace it end to end, from agent behaviour back to the agent infrastructure layer, and fix it You’ve made an improvement to our internal AI tooling that the team now uses day to day The design decisions in your piece have held up under real load, and you can explain the tradeoffs you made and what you’d do differently If these metrics are met, we'd take you full-time without thinking twice Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

description: About us INCO is a leading social enterprise on a mission to shape a more inclusive and sustainable economy that creates opportunities for all. We have teams and programs in over 50 countries. Our work spans five complementary activities: INCO Academy: skilling programs for people facing barriers to employment, leading to careers in fast-growing industries such as technology, sustainability and healthcare (400,000+ job seekers trained to date). INCO Kids: education and awareness programs giving school-age learners future-proof knowledge in technology, sustainability, citizenship and more (350,000+ learners supported to date). INCO Entrepreneurs: incubation and acceleration for underrepresented founders and social entrepreneurs (2,000+ businesses supported every year). INCO Ventures: impact investing and funding for social and environmental impact startups (€500M+ assets under management). INCO Spaces: co-working and co-living spaces for social and environmental innovators (Paris, Berlin, Warsaw and more). About the program: AI and the Future of Work is a new three-year research and policy-engagement program (2026–2029), funded through a research grant partnership and led end to end by INCO. It tracks AI's real-world impact on jobs, tasks and productivity across all 27 EU member states, and gives policymakers the evidence, trend baselines and scenario-planning tools to capture AI's productivity upside while managing the workforce transition. About the role: We are looking for a Senior Program Manager to run the AI and the Future of Work program day to day and make sure it delivers on time, on budget and to the grant's commitments. You will closely lead and collaborate with a Research Lead and a Policy Lead.  You will turn a three-year grant into a working operation: a deliverables calendar across 27 countries, a consortium of up to 15 partners, a publication schedule and a reporting cycle the funder can trust. You need to be comfortable working alongside researchers and policy specialists, and fluent in the rhythm of grant-funded research programs. Responsibilities: Lead program delivery end to end  Planning and implementation Build and own the three-year implementation plan: workstreams, milestones, dependencies and the deliverables calendar agreed with the funder. Run the program's operating rhythm: weekly core-team check-ins, monthly consortium updates and quarterly steering reviews. Coordinate the publication pipeline with the Research and Policy Leads: quarterly data refreshes, five semi-annual reports, policy briefs, the annual flagship and the 2029 EU27 report. Keep thorough program documentation: plans, decision logs, risk register and handover notes. Set up quality-assurance steps for outputs (review cycles, sign-off, editorial and brand checks) together with the Communications team. Run the semi-annual tracking cycle and the reporting calendar for the five P0 markets and five sub-regional clusters, so national and EU27 outputs land together. Monitoring and evaluation Define and track program KPIs and grant deliverables; spot slippage early and agree corrective action with the leads. Collect and compile performance data across workstreams and partners, and report it to your manager and the funder in a structured, actionable way. Coordinate the program's evaluation framework so the team can show what the evidence changed in policy and practice. Budget and resources Own the program budget and cost sheet, including consortium partner budgets and the research consolidation budget held by the Research Lead. Manage timelines and scope so the program delivers within the grant's budget and rules; prepare budget forecasts and reallocation requests. Ensure grant compliance: eligible costs, audit trail, data protection (GDPR) and the funder's reporting requirements, working with Finance and Legal. Manage the consortium and partners  Run the operational side of partner onboarding with the Research Lead: due diligence, contracts, scopes of work, payment schedules and data-sharing agreements. Track the delivery of 8 to 15 national partners against their contracts, and manage underperformance or replacement when needed. Organise consortium working groups, review cycles and annual convenings, and keep communication flowing across countries and time zones. Run the secretariat for the sub-recipient advisory committee (INCO staff, funder representatives and independent experts): schedule meetings, prepare selection materials, record recommendations and keep the process transparent, with final selection resting with INCO. Manage subrecipient compliance: flow-down of grant terms, financial and narrative reporting from partners, and checks before each payment. Manage the funder and stakeholders Act as the primary operational liaison with the grant funder, keeping expectations aligned and surfacing risks early. Prepare and present progress, financial and impact reports to the funder and other key stakeholders. raw.title: Senior Program Manager
raw.description:
About us

INCO is a leading social enterprise on a mission to shape a more inclusive and sustainable economy that creates opportunities for all. We have teams and programs in over 50 countries. Our work spans five complementary activities:

  1. INCO Academy: skilling programs for people facing barriers to employment, leading to careers in fast-growing industries such as technology, sustainability and healthcare (400,000+ job seekers trained to date).

  2. INCO Kids: education and awareness programs giving school-age learners future-proof knowledge in technology, sustainability, citizenship and more (350,000+ learners supported to date).

  3. INCO Entrepreneurs: incubation and acceleration for underrepresented founders and social entrepreneurs (2,000+ businesses supported every year).

  4. INCO Ventures: impact investing and funding for social and environmental impact startups (€500M+ assets under management).

  5. INCO Spaces: co-working and co-living spaces for social and environmental innovators (Paris, Berlin, Warsaw and more).

About the program:

AI and the Future of Work is a new three-year research and policy-engagement program (2026–2029), funded through a research grant partnership and led end to end by INCO. It tracks AI's real-world impact on jobs, tasks and productivity across all 27 EU member states, and gives policymakers the evidence, trend baselines and scenario-planning tools to capture AI's productivity upside while managing the workforce transition.

About the role:

We are looking for a Senior Program Manager to run the AI and the Future of Work program day to day and make sure it delivers on time, on budget and to the grant's commitments. You will closely lead and collaborate with a Research Lead and a Policy Lead. 

You will turn a three-year grant into a working operation: a deliverables calendar across 27 countries, a consortium of up to 15 partners, a publication schedule and a reporting cycle the funder can trust. You need to be comfortable working alongside researchers and policy specialists, and fluent in the rhythm of grant-funded research programs.

Responsibilities:

Lead program delivery end to end 

Planning and implementation

  • Build and own the three-year implementation plan: workstreams, milestones, dependencies and the deliverables calendar agreed with the funder.

  • Run the program's operating rhythm: weekly core-team check-ins, monthly consortium updates and quarterly steering reviews.

  • Coordinate the publication pipeline with the Research and Policy Leads: quarterly data refreshes, five semi-annual reports, policy briefs, the annual flagship and the 2029 EU27 report.

  • Keep thorough program documentation: plans, decision logs, risk register and handover notes.

  • Set up quality-assurance steps for outputs (review cycles, sign-off, editorial and brand checks) together with the Communications team.

  • Run the semi-annual tracking cycle and the reporting calendar for the five P0 markets and five sub-regional clusters, so national and EU27 outputs land together.

Monitoring and evaluation

  • Define and track program KPIs and grant deliverables; spot slippage early and agree corrective action with the leads.

  • Collect and compile performance data across workstreams and partners, and report it to your manager and the funder in a structured, actionable way.

  • Coordinate the program's evaluation framework so the team can show what the evidence changed in policy and practice.

Budget and resources

  • Own the program budget and cost sheet, including consortium partner budgets and the research consolidation budget held by the Research Lead.

  • Manage timelines and scope so the program delivers within the grant's budget and rules; prepare budget forecasts and reallocation requests.

  • Ensure grant compliance: eligible costs, audit trail, data protection (GDPR) and the funder's reporting requirements, working with Finance and Legal.

Manage the consortium and partners 

  • Run the operational side of partner onboarding with the Research Lead: due diligence, contracts, scopes of work, payment schedules and data-sharing agreements.

  • Track the delivery of 8 to 15 national partners against their contracts, and manage underperformance or replacement when needed.

  • Organise consortium working groups, review cycles and annual convenings, and keep communication flowing across countries and time zones.

  • Run the secretariat for the sub-recipient advisory committee (INCO staff, funder representatives and independent experts): schedule meetings, prepare selection materials, record recommendations and keep the process transparent, with final selection resting with INCO.

  • Manage subrecipient compliance: flow-down of grant terms, financial and narrative reporting from partners, and checks before each payment.

Manage the funder and stakeholders

  • Act as the primary operational liaison with the grant funder, keeping expectations aligned and surfacing risks early.

  • Prepare and present progress, financial and impact reports to the funder and other key stakeholders.

  • Work with the Head of Partnerships on funder conversations, renewals and any extension of the partnership.

  • Support the Policy Lead and with the logistics of policymaker convenings, events and launches.

  • Coordinate, with the Policy Lead, the expanded public-engagement activity in Poland and the CEE region, and the logistics of rapid, fact-based responses when AI labour market stories break.

Coordinate the team

  • Set clear responsibilities, timelines and objectives across the core team, and track progress against them.

  • Act as the connecting point between the Research Lead, the Policy Lead, data engineers and INCO's support teams (Communications, Finance, Legal, HR).

  • Identify staffing needs as the program grows (for example research assistants, data roles or a program officer), write job descriptions, interview and onboard new team members, and manage any program staff assigned to you.

Support growth 

  • Work with leadership to standardise how INCO runs grant-funded research programs, so lessons from this one carry over.

  • Identify follow-on funding and adjacent opportunities, for example linking findings to INCO Academy skilling programs.

  • Build relationships across the European research and policy ecosystem.


Essential

  • At least five years managing complex, multi-partner programs, ideally grant-funded research, policy or public-interest programs in Europe.

  • Proven track record managing funders or institutional partners, including donor reporting, budgets and grant compliance.

  • Experience coordinating consortia or networks of external partners, including contracts, scopes of work and partner payments.

  • At least four years leading teams and working cross-functionally, including with senior experts you do not line manage.

  • Strong budget and financial management skills, with ownership of program cost sheets and forecasts.

  • High digital collaboration literacy (Slack, Monday.com, Notion, G-Suite or similar) and comfort running remote work across many countries.

  • Professional English, written and spoken.

  • Strong attention to detail and organisational skills, with excellent communication, versatility and integrity.

Desirable

  • Experience with EU-funded or foundation-funded research programs (for example Horizon Europe, Erasmus+ or major philanthropic grants).

  • Familiarity with research operations: publication cycles, data protection (GDPR), research ethics and data-sharing agreements.

  • Interest in AI, the labour market, skills or the future of work; familiarity with EU institutions such as Cedefop, Eurostat, Eurofound or the JRC.

  • A second EU language, especially German, French, Spanish, Italian or Polish.

  • A recognised project management certification (for example PMP or PRINCE2).

  • Experience managing sub-grants or sub-recipients, including selection processes and flow-down compliance.

  • Bearbeitung und Nachverfolgung von Security-Tickets über Jira (perspektivisch ServiceNow) sowie Einsatz von Tufin SecureTrack im Netzwerk-Sicherheitsmanagement

Womit du bei uns glänzt

  • Du verfügst über Grundkenntnisse in der Administration von Windows- und Linux-Servern und bist mit der Netzwerktechnik vertraut

  • Du kannst mit IT-Security-Zertifizierungen wie Microsoft SC-200, CompTIA Security+, CySA+ oder Fortinet-Zertifizierungen zusätzlich punkten

  • Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und gut auf Englisch - im Team, mit Kund:innen und im Alltag

Darauf kannst du dich freuen

Bei uns bekommst du mehr als nur einen Job. Wir wollen, dass du dich weiterentwickeln, wohlfühlen und mitgestalten kannst. Hier ein paar Gründe, warum du gerne bei uns arbeitest:

  • Mehr Freiheit: 30 Tage Urlaub, flexible Arbeitszeiten mit Orientierung an unseren Servicezeiten (7–17 Uhr) und bis zu 25 Tage arbeiten im EU-Ausland

  • Arbeiten, wie es zu dir passt: Ob im Büro oder von zuhause - du entscheidest, was für dich am besten funktioniert

  • Gutes Arbeitsumfeld: Moderne Technik und klare Strukturen

  • Sichere und faire Konditionen: attraktives Gehalt, JobRad, betriebliche Altersvorsorge und Unterstützung über meinEAP, unser kostenloses Beratungsangebot - auch für deine Familie

Vielfalt macht uns stärker - deshalb fördern wir bewusst ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem alle Menschen willkommen sind.
Unabhängig von sozialer oder ethnischer Herkunft, Geschlecht, Alter, Religion oder Weltanschauung, Behinderung, sexueller Identität und Orientierung: Wir bieten allen Bewerbenden einen fairen Prozess und gerechte Chancen. Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen von Menschen, die unsere Haltung zu Vielfalt, Gleichberechtigung und Inklusion teilen – und Lust haben, gemeinsam mit uns eine inklusive Arbeitswelt zu gestalten.

title: Sr. Software Engineer, Full Stack (EDI)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Who We Are</strong></span></p> <p>Addepar is a global data and AI platform empowering investment professionals to turn complex financial information into actionable intelligence. Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. More than 1,500 firms in 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $10 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and levels of complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, London, Edinburgh, Geneva, Warsaw, Dubai, Pune and Singapore.</p></div><h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>The Role</strong></span></h4> <p>The Workflow Platform team builds Addepar's orchestration layer: a platform, on top of Temporal, that lets other Addepar teams turn long-running, multi-step business processes (approvals, data operations, reporting, client notifications) into reliable, observable, human-in-the-loop workflows. As part of the platform offering we own: Task Centre, where users act on the work workflows assign to them; the Executions view, where teams monitor and manage running workflows; and Client Notifications.</p> <p>We're adding a senior full-stack engineer in Edinburgh. To begin with you'll mostly work on the user-facing side of the platform, and you'll also work on the services behind it. Our engineers work across the stack and in more than one language. Whichever side is newer to you, we'll give you real work there and the support to grow into it. You'll be given high-impact projects to lead end to end, such as a new Task Centre surface, the Executions view, or the components product teams use to build their own task types. You'll work closely with Product and Design to shape what we build, and with our Staff-level tech lead on how we build it, alongside colleagues in Pune and the US and the product teams building on the platform.</p> <p>Applicants must have, and maintain, the right to work in the United Kingdom from the first day of employment. Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this role.<strong><br></strong></p> <h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>What You’ll Do</strong></span></h4> <ul> <li>Own the design and delivery of a defined area of the platform end to end, from interface to API: write the design, break it into deliverable slices, ship it and support it in production.</li> <li>Build user-facing features in React and TypeScript that make complex, long-running workflows clear and actionable for the people working in them.</li> <li>Work on the services behind those experiences (Python and Java APIs and workflow workers), and shape API contracts so the front end and back end evolve together.</li> <li>Make the platform easier for other teams to build on: reusable UI components and patterns, clear contracts, and documentation that lets them self-serve.</li> <li>Spot gaps and opportunities in your area and act on them without waiting for direction.</li> <li>Write RFCs for your area, present them at our weekly Architecture Working Group, and contribute to design reviews of others' work.</li> <li>Share in running what we build: observability, debugging live issues, incident response and our on-call rotation.</li> <li>Share what you know with less-experienced engineers through code review, pairing and design discussion.</li> <li>Help the team use AI-assisted development effectively and responsibly.</li> </ul> <h4><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Who You Are</strong></span></h4> <ul> <li>Extensive software engineering experience, much of it building web front ends, with a track record of taking features from design to production.</li> <li>Strong in TypeScript and a modern component framework (we use React), including state management, data fetching and testing UI code.</li> <li>Has worked on the backend of products they've built (APIs, data models, services) in any language, and wants to do more of it.</li> <li>Cares about usability and accessibility. Can turn a rough requirement into an interface people can use without a manual, with or without a finished design.</li> <li>Designs UIs for systems that are slow, asynchronous or failing: loading, partial and error states, retries and stale data.</li> <li>Makes and owns decisions in their area, including when established processes don't fully fit.</li> <li>Finds and closes gaps in their area without waiting to be told.</li> <li>Collaborates across teams without a manager driving alignment, and uses clear reasoning and evidence to influence decisions in their area.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Our Values&nbsp;</strong></span></p> <ul> <li><strong>Act Like an Owner - </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">Think and operate with intention, purpose and care. Own outcomes.</span></li> <li><strong>Build Together - </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">Collaborate to unlock the best solutions. Deliver lasting value.&nbsp;</span></li> <li><strong>Champion Our Clients - </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">Exceed client expectations. Our clients’ success is our success.&nbsp;</span></li> <li><strong>Drive Innovation - </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">Be bold and unconstrained in problem solving. Transform the industry.&nbsp;</span></li> <li><strong>Embrace Learning - </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">Engage our community to broaden our perspective. title: Senior Network Engineer - Low Latency Trading
description:
<p>The Networks team designs, builds and maintains all the communications infrastructure that allows our high-capacity, low-latency trading and data research environments to run 24/7.&nbsp; This network spans over 25 countries and 100 locations. We are looking for a Senior Network Engineer with experience designing and managing large environments to fulfill the high-performance and availability requirements of a premiere algorithmic trading firm operating in global financial markets.&nbsp;</p> <p>This position requires both project management and deep technical skills. Working together with some of the brightest minds in our industry, you’ll be responsible for everything from product selection and design to routing configuration and troubleshooting. You will work closely with our Systems and Trading Operations teams as well as others at HRT to build, manage, and monitor our low-latency trading network. You’ll have broad responsibilities with freedom to analyze and solve problems, and your solutions will have an immediate impact on our worldwide operations.&nbsp;</p> <p>We’re looking for someone with a love for technology and an excitement for tackling big picture problems. You will work on a wide variety of projects to enhance the performance and capacity of the global trading and research platforms and contribute to both high-level strategy and the technical nitty-gritty of our global network architecture.</p> <p><strong>Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related IT field</li> <li>5-10 years of relevant experience, preferably in low-latency and high-frequency trading environments.</li> <li>In depth understanding of common layer 2 and layer 3 network protocols and best practices; working knowledge of OSPF, BGP, PIM, IGMP</li> <li>Experience managing Arista, Cisco, and other common networking devices on a day-to-day basis</li> <li>Familiarity with low-latency microwave networks and/or optical transmission systems, such as Adva, Ciena is desirable</li> <li>Experience in designing enterprise networks, capacity planning, and full lifecycle project management</li> <li>Experience with packet decoding and analysis tools such as tcpdump and Wireshark</li> <li>Excellent oral and written communication skills: able to distill complicated issues into clear and concise terms and to create and maintain effective technical documentation</li> <li>Experience with Unix/Linux command line utilities and networking stack</li> <li>Excellent troubleshooting skills on a wide range of networking issues, including common ethernet LAN problems, multicast market data distribution, and global WAN</li> <li>Understanding of basic power consumption and cooling issues in a datacenter environment</li> <li>Knowledge of fiber optics technology and cabling standards. Ability to sort through specs and make recommendations on appropriate purchases</li> <li>Willingness and ability to solve small technical problems in the field yourself.</li> <li>You have excellent collaboration skills and a willingness to admit mistakes.</li> <li>Familiarity with firewalls (including Cisco, Palo Alto, Fortinet), VPNs and NAT</li> <li>Familiarity with configuration management tools, such as Ansible or Salt is desirable</li> <li>Familiarity with Python, Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, GitHub is desirable</li> <li>Familiarity with public cloud networks, such as AWS, GCP, Azure, is desirable</li> </ul> <p>The estimated base salary range for this position is 200,000 to 300,000 USD per year (or local equivalent). title: AI Research Engineer
description:
<p>Hudson River Trading (HRT) is seeking an AI Research Engineer to join the HAIL team. HAIL (HRT AI Labs) is the team at HRT responsible for developing and maintaining our most powerful models, which are used by our trading teams to drive a significant fraction of our trading. We are building and deploying "foundation models for markets", that ingest and train on vast amounts of market and “alternative” data (such as language) to make predictions about future market state.</p> <p>As a research engineer on HAIL, you will have a general mandate to improve all aspects of large-scale model training, including but not limited to kernel development, training data loading, parallelism, networking, and fault-tolerance. You will work closely with our researchers to co-design and improve our models, and shape the research agenda.</p> <p>We have multiple large, modern, and rapidly growing GPU clusters, and we maintain a very high GPU-to-researcher ratio. We are simultaneously pursuing multiple strategies and developing many model types with different purposes, and we are strongly incentivized to squeeze as much as we can out of our systems. Your work will be directly, clearly, and highly impactful on the business, and it will be challenging: this is a field with no easy or obvious solutions.</p> <p><strong>Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Strong engineering skills, especially any of: CUDA/Triton/Pallas/CuTe DSL kernel development, lower-level PyTorch/JAX/XLA development, CUDA Graphs, FPGA/ASIC experience</li> <li>Must have two or more years work experience building deep learning systems, for any domain: language, speech, robotics, biology, chemistry, physics, audio, video, recommendations, etc.</li> <li>Experience translating methods between areas of application is highly valued</li> <li>Must be comfortable writing PyTorch or JAX code</li> <li>Deep learning research experience is valuable, but not necessary</li> <li>LLM experience is valuable, but not necessary</li> <li>Finance experience is not required</li> </ul> <p>The estimated base salary range for this position is 250,000 to 300,000 USD per year (or local equivalent). title: Software Implementation Project Manager
description: About 3E: 3E is a mission-driven company dedicated to creating a safer and more sustainable world. We offer award-winning regulatory intelligence and AI solutions to help organizations protect people and products. With over 35 years of experience and a global presence, we empower our customers with innovative compliance solutions. You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges. Join us and make an impact! About the Role As an Implementation Project Manager at 3E, you’ll lead larger, more complex customer implementations where successful delivery requires multiple products, technical contributors, workstreams, dependencies, and stakeholders to operate against one coordinated plan. You’ll be accountable for turning the customer’s scope of work into an executable implementation strategy and for determining whether the overall project succeeds—on time, within scope, adopted, and connected to a clear customer outcome. You’ll establish success and acceptance criteria, own the integrated project plan, manage risk and change, coordinate specialists and technical teams, and give both customers and 3E leadership a clear, data-backed view of project health. You’ll understand the technical delivery deeply enough to challenge assumptions, identify dependencies, connect customer needs with the right specialists, and engage credibly with Product and Engineering. You won’t need to personally execute every configuration, migration, or integration; your role is to ensure those pieces come together into a successful customer outcome. What You’ll Do Lead complex new-logo, cross-sell, and Value Realization implementations from internal handoff through customer acceptance and formal close. Translate complex scopes of work into an integrated delivery strategy covering products, workstreams, milestones, resources, dependencies, assumptions, exclusions, and acceptance criteria. Lead technical discovery and pre-integration planning with customers, CX technical specialists, and relevant internal teams. Own the master implementation plan and coordinate implementation specialists, Product, Engineering, Data, Cloud, technical consultants, external partners, and customer resources. Establish measurable success and acceptance criteria at kickoff and maintain accountability for those outcomes throughout delivery. Lead customer project governance, including senior stakeholder and sponsor communications. Maintain the milestone tracker and conduct phase-gate reviews, giving a clear assessment of whether projects are on track, at risk, or behind and establishing mitigation plans when required. Identify cross-workstream dependencies and risks early and determine their impact on the critical path. Lead complex, multi-product delivery by managing scope and change control, coordinating custom development through launch, maintaining a unified customer plan across teams, and providing leadership with clear, data-backed reporting on project health, risk, timelines, value, and adoption. Build and maintain dashboards or reporting tools that make project status and risks visible without relying solely on status meetings. Lead customer escalations diplomatically while maintaining accountability for customer commitments, decisions, resources, data readiness, and signoffs. Partner with Commercial on implementation handoff and identify expansion opportunities or renewal risks surfaced during delivery. Represent the delivery perspective during pre-sales scoping of complex or higher-risk opportunities so commitments can be successfully delivered. Drive structured post-onboarding Value Realization Projects, including complex migrations, integrations, optimization, remediation, and workflow initiatives. Manage multiple concurrent implementations and make prioritization decisions based on risk, complexity, dependencies, and customer impact. Identify opportunities to improve implementation processes, delivery predictability, time-to-value, and the overall customer experience. What Makes You a Great Fit Required 3–5 years of experience in software implementation, customer onboarding, technical account or project management, or professional services, ideally within B2B SaaS, technology, or information services. Experience with SAP EHS implementation is required. Demonstrated experience leading complex customer implementations with multiple workstreams, technical dependencies, contributors, or products. Experience owning project scope, plans, milestones, risks, dependencies, change control, customer communication, and delivery outcomes. Strong technical aptitude and the ability to understand configuration, data, integration, and technical delivery sufficiently to coordinate specialists and identify risk; coding is not required. A large share of every engagement is data engineering: ingestion, flattening deeply nested structures, extracting content from unstructured documents, classification, summarisation, tagging, enrichment, indexing.   • Senior FDE: 5+ years engineering, 2+ years AI or agentic AI, has owned the architecture of at least one production agent system end-to-end and led a client conversation about it.

This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who combines deep technical expertise with strong commercial judgement and can apply both to Monzo’s most important and complex challenges.</p> <p>At Monzo, we’re building a bank that is fair, transparent and a delight to use. We’re growing extremely fast and have over 11 million customers in the UK. We’ve built a product that people love and more than 80% of our growth comes from word of mouth and referrals.</p> <p><em>Enable Monzo to Make Better Decisions, Faster</em></p> <p>We have a strong culture of data-driven decision making across the whole company. And we’re great believers in powerful, real-time analytics and empowerment of the wider business. You’ll apply judgement in areas of organisational or technical complexity, steward initiatives end-to-end, and focus your hands-on contribution where it can create the greatest impact. You’ll be a trusted technical partner to senior leaders, raise the bar for Data Science across Monzo, and build capability in others through coaching, reusable approaches and clear standards.</p> <h4><strong>Our Data Science team ⭐</strong></h4> <p>We are excited to be expanding and are hiring across our Data Science teams. Whether your interests lie in Borrowing, Growth, Payments, Fincrime, Wealth or Core, we are looking for versatile people who can contribute across squads and collectives. While we allocate teams after the interview process, we aim to match your skills and aspirations with the most suitable role. Throughout the process, you will meet team members from across our Data Science collectives, who will guide you through the opportunities available. Join us and be part of shaping our future!</p> <h4><strong>🔑You’ll play a key role by...</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Shape and lead the data strategy for a large domain or collective, connecting customer and commercial goals to a clear portfolio of high-impact Data Science work</li> <li>Identify, frame and lead strategically important problems where the path is ambiguous, dependencies span teams, and decisions involve meaningful customer, commercial, regulatory or operational trade-offs</li> <li>Partner with senior leaders across product, engineering, ML, design, research, risk and operations, bringing an independent technical perspective that influences strategy and turns it into measurable outcomes</li> <li>Establish measurement strategies and metric maps that clarify how customer behaviour, product changes and business outcomes connect, enabling teams to test assumptions and make better decisions faster</li> <li>Set and evolve best practices for experimentation, causal inference, forecasting, optimisation and decision science, choosing methods that are proportionate to the decision and its risks</li> <li>Remain hands-on where your expertise is most valuable: exploring complex data, designing analyses and experiments, building models or prototypes, and resolving the hardest technical questions</li> <li>Steward critical data products and initiatives end-to-end, ensuring they are robust, well-governed, clearly documented and adopted by the people who need them</li> <li>Balance pace and analytical rigour, making pragmatic trade-offs while protecting the quality, reproducibility and interpretability of your work</li> <li>Raise Data Science standards across Monzo through technical direction, proposals, reviews, reusable methods and thoughtful challenge</li> <li>Coach and mentor data scientists and analytics engineers, using live projects and wider discipline initiatives to build sustainable capability beyond your own individual output</li> </ul> <h4><strong>🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…</strong></h4> <ul> <li>You have an exceptional track record of leading complex, business-critical Data Science work from ambiguous and hold a consistently high bar for analytical quality, governance and reproducibility</li> <li>You remain a highly credible hands-on practitioner with SQL and Python, while raising standards and multiplying the impact of experienced colleagues</li> </ul> <p><strong>The interview process:</strong></p> <p>Our interview process involves:</p> <ul> <li>Recruiter Call</li> <li>Initial Call</li> weeks, but we will always work around your availability. At Checkout.com , the Cloud Platform team owns the cloud foundations that global payments depend on: a large multi-account AWS estate, a growing Azure platform, and the networking and connectivity that reaches card schemes and banks worldwide. We are building a platform that lets product teams run across multiple clouds and regions. We are looking for a Senior Technical Programme Manager who can turn a complex, multi-team technical programme into a plan people trust and deliver against. This is a senior role in an established, fast-moving team. You will own the multi-cloud and multi-region programme end to end: the plan, the dependencies, the risks and the roadmap. As a Senior Technical Programme Manager, you are responsible for delivering the programme across teams you don't manage. You will work closely with your Engineering Manager to shape direction, manage dependencies across pillars, and ensure the programme meets the standards a regulated payments business demands. Clear written and verbal communication with senior stakeholders Proven ability to get commitments from teams and leaders who don't report to you. Experience in a regulated environment, such as financial services or payments How you’ll make an impact: Run the programme end to end, from sequencing the work through to production, across several teams and multiple cloud providers. Use AI tools in how you run the programme: status reporting, dependency analysis, drafting and keeping documentation current. We use them heavily and expect you to as well. Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands. We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here. description: <h2>Opportunity</h2> <p>Brunswick is accelerating its use of AI to strengthen the advice we give clients and how we operate. We are looking for a Data Architect to join our AI Lab and shape the technical and data foundations that enable us to build and scale proprietary AI products securely and effectively.</p> <p>This is a hands-on, influential role spanning architecture and practical delivery. You will take a portfolio-wide view of how data, applications, models, APIs and shared components fit together, creating reusable patterns and capabilities that help engineers move faster while maintaining high standards of security, resilience and maintainability.</p> <p>Working closely with AI Engineers, Infrastructure, Security, Data and other technology teams, you will ensure the Lab has the architecture and underlying platform it needs to innovate at pace while aligning with Brunswick’s wider technology environment.</p> <h2>About the Role</h2> <p>Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:</p> <ul> <li>Design and evolve the data and technical architecture underpinning the AI Lab’s portfolio of proprietary products.</li> <li>Define scalable patterns for how applications, data sources, models, APIs and enterprise systems connect and interact.</li> <li>Design approaches to data modelling, access, storage, movement and governance, particularly for sensitive or business-critical information.</li> <li>Identify opportunities to create reusable services, components and data capabilities that accelerate development across multiple products.</li> <li>Establish standards and patterns for data pipelines, APIs, integration, environments, deployment and observability.</li> <li>Work closely with engineers to translate architectural principles into practical solutions, balancing scalability with rapid prototyping and delivery.</li> <li>Partner with Infrastructure, Security, Data and other technology teams to ensure solutions meet Brunswick’s security, privacy, governance and architectural standards.</li> <li>Identify opportunities to simplify the data landscape, reduce duplication and improve interoperability across the firm.</li> <li>Evaluate emerging technologies and architectural approaches that could strengthen the Lab’s platform or unlock new capabilities.</li> <li>Help build the scalable data foundations Brunswick needs to develop and deploy AI responsibly, securely and effectively.</li> </ul> <h2>What We’re Looking For</h2> <p>You will combine strong data and solution architecture skills with a practical engineering mindset and the ability to operate in a fast-moving product environment. You will be comfortable moving between strategic architecture and detailed technical decisions, making pragmatic trade-offs between long-term scalability and speed of delivery. The successful candidate will bring:</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>6+ years of relevant experience in data architecture, solution architecture, data engineering, software engineering or a related technical role.</li> <li>Strong experience designing scalable data and application architectures, ideally in cloud environments.</li> <li>Experience designing data models, APIs, integrations and data flows across databases, SaaS applications and enterprise systems.</li> <li>Strong knowledge of modern data architecture, including data modelling, ETL/ELT pipelines, storage, access patterns, data warehouses, lakes/lakehouses and governance.</li> <li>Experience with cloud platforms; Microsoft Azure experience is particularly relevant.</li> <li>Good working knowledge of SQL and modern data engineering approaches, including Python.</li> <li>Experience designing reusable technical components, shared services or platforms used across multiple products or teams.</li> <li>A strong understanding of data governance, security, privacy, lineage and quality, and how these are embedded into architecture and delivery.</li> <li>An understanding of the data requirements of AI and machine-learning applications, including securely making structured and unstructured enterprise data available to AI solutions.</li> <li>A good understanding of modern software engineering and SDLC practices, including CI/CD, version control, testing and observability.</li> <li>Sufficient hands-on technical depth to work credibly with engineers, review designs and contribute to implementation where useful.</li> <li>Strong judgement and pragmatism, with the ability to balance consistency and reuse with experimentation and speed.</li> <li>Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to explain architectural decisions and trade-offs to technical and non-technical colleagues.</li> </ul> <p>Desirable experience</p> <ul> <li>Architecting applications or platforms incorporating generative AI, large language models or machine learning.</li> <li>Designing data and integration architectures for AI applications, including retrieval and grounding approaches.</li> <li>Building internal developer platforms, shared services or reusable application frameworks.</li> <li>Working with sensitive enterprise data and complex security or governance requirements.</li> <li>Experience in professional services, financial services, advisory or another complex enterprise environment.</li> </ul> <h2>Why Join Us</h2> <p>Whether you are joining a client facing team, a core services team, or starting out on your professional career journey, joining Brunswick unlocks a range of employee benefits to support your financial future, health and wellness, family and community and continuous professional development.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h1>About Brunswick</h1> <p>Brunswick is a global advisory firm. We help companies tackle high-stakes issues, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, and deliver high-impact outcomes.&nbsp;</p> <p>Our clients value our ability to anticipate, shape, and respond to the key players and forces in the financial and investment arena, regulatory and geopolitical universe, NGO community, workforce and beyond. They rely on us for deep experience, fresh perspectives and original thinking. So, in Brunswick you will find an exceptional range of experience and talent with a rich mix of backgrounds. From the beginning, we have prioritized attracting, developing, and retaining the best professionals in the industry, united by a culture of inclusivity, excellence, and intellectual curiosity.</p> <p>Founded in 1987 in London, the firm has organically grown to 27 offices in 18 countries across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Australia. We operate as a “one-firm firm” with no individual profit centers. This allows us to assemble fully integrated, bespoke teams for each client, able to draw on the full resources of Brunswick anywhere in the world.&nbsp;</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><em>Brunswick is an equal opportunity employer. &nbsp;All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law. Please&nbsp;read our <a href="https://www.brunswickgroup.com/app/uploads/Group-Privacy-Notice-for-Employees_April-2026.pdf" target="_blank">Global Privacy Notice</a> to understand how your data is managed.</em></p> <p>&nbsp;</p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Whether it's a push notification, social campaign, or packaging design—we craft compelling experiences that shape perceptions, spark engagement, and make Deliveroo a loved, global brand.

What You'll Be Doing

You'll be joining the Integrated Marketing team. We own the Deliveroo brand globally and lead our biggest campaign moments. Working in a cross-functional squad alongside strategic teams, functional leads, and local markets, we turn big ideas into high-impact campaigns across our markets.

  • Global Campaign Ownership: Lead high-profile global marketing programmes and integrated campaigns from global strategy through to local market execution.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner closely with cross-functional squads, strategic teams, functional leads, and local market leads to align campaign strategies with core business goals.

  • Stakeholder Management: Influence senior stakeholders across the global organisation without direct authority, ensuring alignment on messaging, execution, and performance metrics.

  • Strategic Optimisation: Balance tactical execution with a longer-term strategic perspective to solve complex marketing briefs and continuously optimize brand performance.

What You'll Need to Thrive

Essential

  • Integrated Brand Leadership: Proven experience leading end-to-end global integrated marketing campaigns from initial strategy through to local market activation.

  • Framework Development: Strong track record in establishing measurement frameworks, campaign playbooks, and operational systems that scale across multiple regions.

  • Stakeholder Influence: Demonstrated ability to influence and align senior cross-functional stakeholders and matrix teams without direct line management authority.

  • Strategic & Tactical Execution: Proven ability to operate independently on complex or ambiguous briefs, balancing day-to-day execution with longer-term brand strategy.

  • Commercial Acumen: Strong expertise in linking brand initiatives and marketing campaigns directly to measurable business growth and commercial impact.

Nice to Have

  • Experience navigating three-sided marketplace dynamics or fast-paced consumer tech environments.

  • Background working across international or multi-market structures.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving.

We're food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

Your work directly improves experiences for customers, partners and riders.

🌱 Learn fast in an entrepreneurial environment

Work close to the market with autonomy, pace and real responsibility.

Stretch yourself, develop new skills and grow as the business evolves.

Collaborative, values-driven teams that support how you work best.

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Find more about how we hire here.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

title: Enterprise Account Executive
description: SingleStore is looking for an accomplished sales professional to join our Sales Team. AI is moving from experimentation into production, and this role is an opportunity to break into AI while doing meaningful enterprise selling. As an Account Executive, AI Hunter, your job is simple: create new SingleStore customers. You will find companies building AI applications where data access, real-time context, memory, retrieval, or operational scale is becoming a constraint—and turn those challenges into new SingleStore customers. You will own a broad territory, build a majority self-sourced pipeline, create demand in an emerging category, and close greenfield enterprise opportunities. This is a true hunting role. You will engage customers before they have a defined project, develop customer-specific points of view, create urgency around business and technical problems, work with technical experts to land first production workloads, and build a measurable new-logo business with broad ownership. The ideal candidate is a measurable enterprise hunter who is competitive, curious, technically credible, resilient, and able to sell business outcomes. Direct AI sales experience is valuable, but proven selling ability and technical curiosity matter more than a narrow "AI seller" title. Role and Responsibilities Build and execute a territory strategy for net-new customer acquisition. Prospect fearlessly across a broad account universe using proactive, persistent outbound, account-based, partner, and market-education motions; stay resilient and effective through rejection and ambiguity. Form account hypotheses, map the buying center, and earn first meetings with relevant points of view tailored to the customer. Engage executive, business, technical, security, and procurement stakeholders. Lead great business-first discovery, connect AI and data challenges to fundable goals, and build quantified ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases. Build and develop champions, multi-thread the buying group, earn executive and economic-buyer access, and maintain stakeholder alignment; own the stakeholder plan, mutual action plan, close plan, value case, stage gates, forecast, and commercial outcome. Lead complex sales cycles through technical validation, security, legal, procurement, negotiation, and close. Partner with Solutions and Forward Deployment Engineers and cross-functional teams to validate technical fit and establish the first production workload. Navigate competitive displacement and maintain disciplined activity management, CRM hygiene, reporting, qualification, forecasting, and opportunity management; showcase clear metrics such as pipeline created, meetings, conversion, quota attainment, and new-logo performance. Be AI fluent: use AI and research tools productively and responsibly while applying judgment, validating outputs, and separating facts from hypotheses. Travel within the assigned territory as required.  Required Skills and Experience 5+ years of quota-carrying B2B enterprise software sales experience, ideally selling to large or technically sophisticated organizations; experience in data, cloud, analytics, AI, or adjacent technical domains is a plus. Repeated, quantified quota success with clear ownership of new-logo wins and self-sourced pipeline. Experience closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals involving executives, technical evaluators, security, legal, finance, procurement, and partners. Ability to sell measurable business outcomes and build ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases. Technical fluency in an adjacent domain such as databases, data infrastructure, analytics, AI/ML, cloud, Kubernetes, developer tools, cybersecurity, observability, or open-source software. Strong qualification, account planning, forecasting, CRM, negotiation, and deal-management skills. Learning velocity and coachability, demonstrated through specific behavior change after feedback; ability to explain technical concepts clearly to technical and executive audiences. Executive presence, customer trust, resilience, intellectual honesty, and excellent communication skills. B.A., B.S. degree or equivalent in a related field. Experience with Fortune 500 or security-sensitive organizations, cloud ecosystems, open-source or consumption-based products, or emerging categories is preferred. raw.description:
SingleStore is looking for an accomplished sales professional to join our Sales Team. AI is moving from experimentation into production, and this role is an opportunity to break into AI while doing meaningful enterprise selling.

As an Account Executive, AI Hunter, your job is simple: create new SingleStore customers. You will find companies building AI applications where data access, real-time context, memory, retrieval, or operational scale is becoming a constraint—and turn those challenges into new SingleStore customers. You will own a broad territory, build a majority self-sourced pipeline, create demand in an emerging category, and close greenfield enterprise opportunities.

This is a true hunting role. You will engage customers before they have a defined project, develop customer-specific points of view, create urgency around business and technical problems, work with technical experts to land first production workloads, and build a measurable new-logo business with broad ownership. The ideal candidate is a measurable enterprise hunter who is competitive, curious, technically credible, resilient, and able to sell business outcomes. Direct AI sales experience is valuable, but proven selling ability and technical curiosity matter more than a narrow "AI seller" title.

Role and Responsibilities

  • Build and execute a territory strategy for net-new customer acquisition.
  • Prospect fearlessly across a broad account universe using proactive, persistent outbound, account-based, partner, and market-education motions; stay resilient and effective through rejection and ambiguity.
  • Form account hypotheses, map the buying center, and earn first meetings with relevant points of view tailored to the customer.
  • Engage executive, business, technical, security, and procurement stakeholders.
  • Lead great business-first discovery, connect AI and data challenges to fundable goals, and build quantified ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases.
  • Build and develop champions, multi-thread the buying group, earn executive and economic-buyer access, and maintain stakeholder alignment; own the stakeholder plan, mutual action plan, close plan, value case, stage gates, forecast, and commercial outcome.
  • Lead complex sales cycles through technical validation, security, legal, procurement, negotiation, and close.
  • Partner with Solutions and Forward Deployment Engineers and cross-functional teams to validate technical fit and establish the first production workload.
  • Navigate competitive displacement and maintain disciplined activity management, CRM hygiene, reporting, qualification, forecasting, and opportunity management; showcase clear metrics such as pipeline created, meetings, conversion, quota attainment, and new-logo performance.
  • Be AI fluent: use AI and research tools productively and responsibly while applying judgment, validating outputs, and separating facts from hypotheses.
  • Travel within the assigned territory as required. 

Required Skills and Experience

  • 5+ years of quota-carrying B2B enterprise software sales experience, ideally selling to large or technically sophisticated organizations; experience in data, cloud, analytics, AI, or adjacent technical domains is a plus.
  • Repeated, quantified quota success with clear ownership of new-logo wins and self-sourced pipeline.
  • Experience closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals involving executives, technical evaluators, security, legal, finance, procurement, and partners.
  • Ability to sell measurable business outcomes and build ROI, TCO, or operational-impact cases.
  • Technical fluency in an adjacent domain such as databases, data infrastructure, analytics, AI/ML, cloud, Kubernetes, developer tools, cybersecurity, observability, or open-source software.
  • Strong qualification, account planning, forecasting, CRM, negotiation, and deal-management skills.
  • Learning velocity and coachability, demonstrated through specific behavior change after feedback; ability to explain technical concepts clearly to technical and executive audiences.
  • Executive presence, customer trust, resilience, intellectual honesty, and excellent communication skills.
  • B.A., B.S. degree or equivalent in a related field.
  • Experience with Fortune 500 or security-sensitive organizations, cloud ecosystems, open-source or consumption-based products, or emerging categories is preferred.

title: Senior Frontend Engineer
description: About Us Plentific is a property technology platform used by housing providers, local authorities, housing associations, asset managers, and contractors across the UK and Germany to coordinate repairs, maintenance, and contractor workflows at scale. The platform combines a marketplace, workflow automation, and operational analytics, and is built to handle the volume and compliance demands of social housing, local authority property portfolios, and large-scale residential operations. We are headquartered in London and our team works across Europe. We are growing the team to expand the platform's coverage across Europe and to integrate AI throughout the product and operating model. If you are interested in working on hard, real-world problems in a sector that has long been under-served by good software, we would like to hear from you. The Role We are hiring a Senior Frontend Engineer to build the product surfaces that housing providers, contractors, and residents use every day. This is a fully remote position; we currently have remote engineers based in the UK, Germany, Turkey, Poland, Italy, Spain, and Portugal. You will report to a Team Lead, a hands-on engineer who still writes code and has a small number of engineers reporting to them, and work alongside product managers, designers, backend engineers, and data analysts. Our frontend is built on TypeScript, React, React Router, TanStack Query, MaterialUI and BaseUI, against an increasingly service-oriented backend built in Django REST Framework and PostgreSQL. The codebase is large but clean, because we put real weight on design patterns, readability, testability, maintainability, and extendability. The engineering team sits at the centre of what Plentific does, and the problems are genuinely difficult: online payments, quoting, invoicing, booking, search and scoring algorithms, in-app messaging, real-time notifications, and fraud prevention. Much of it is high-volume and messy legacy integrations, complex permissions, strict compliance requirements, and users who need software to fit how work actually happens on the ground. We expect you to apply engineering judgement to these problems rather than only writing the code in front of you, and to treat agentic, spec-driven development as a normal part of how you work rather than an experiment. Success in this role means shipping interfaces that are fast, accessible, and well-tested, raising the standard of the frontend codebase around you, and leaving the engineers you work with better than you found them. Key Responsibilities Frontend Engineering Build and maintain product interfaces in TypeScript, React, TanStack Query, React Router, MaterialUI and BaseUI across our web applications. Translate product requirements and design concepts into technical documents that set out scope, system behaviour, edge cases, and high-level technical analysis. Design component APIs, state management, and data-fetching patterns that stay readable and extendable as the codebase grows. Integrate against REST APIs in a service-oriented architecture, shaping the contracts with backend engineers rather than accepting whatever is offered. Review, refactor, and retire existing code so it meets the requirements of improved or new features. Review and improve our development workflows, continuous integration checks, deployment pipelines and infrastructure. Keep up to date with technology and bring in new standards and practices for improved user or developer experience Performance, Quality, and Reliability Diagnose and resolve page load, rendering, and other frontend performance problems. Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests that give the team confidence to ship frequently. Instrument frontend observability with tools such as Sentry, Grafana Logs or New Relic, and act on what they show. Debug and fix production issues across our applications, including the integration points where frontend and backend behaviour diverge. Design against common frontend security risks, including XSS and CSRF. Agentic and Spec-Driven Development Turn ambiguous product ideas into implementation-ready specs, including user flows, component behaviour, edge cases, acceptance criteria, and test expectations. Prototype interfaces and interaction quickly, using working software to test feasibility and product value before committing to larger delivery. Use agentic coding tools such as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent to generate, refactor, test, and review code within clear technical constraints. Evaluate AI-generated code critically for correctness, maintainability, security, performance, accessibility, and fit with Plentific's architecture. Improve the team's spec-driven development practice through reusable prompt patterns, review checklists, examples, and lightweight documentation. Collaboration and Craft Partner with product managers, designers, and backend engineers from problem framing through release, applying engineering judgement to improve the user experience before implementation starts. Collaborate with other engineers through code review and pair programming. Define and communicate frontend standards and best practices, and hold the team to them in review. Write concise technical documentation covering components, algorithms, APIs, and operational handover. Articulate technical trade-offs in plain English to technical and non-technical colleagues, including when scope, quality, or delivery timing needs to change. Requirements Expert-level TypeScript and modern JavaScript, with deep command of React and the patterns around it, including data fetching, routing, and component libraries. Strong software engineering fundamentals, including design patterns, testing, debugging, and code that stays readable and extendable at scale. Sound grasp of UI, UX and accessibility considerations, with the judgement to improve a design before building it rather than implement it exactly as drawn. Demonstrable experience diagnosing and fixing page load, rendering, and other frontend performance problems. Working knowledge of frontend observability with Sentry, Grafana logs, or New Relic, and of CI/CD pipelines such as GitHub Actions or ArgoCD. Working knowledge of frontend observability with Sentry, Grafana logs, New Relic or other tools used to monitor, diagnose and fix issues Hands-on background with CI/CD tooling (e.g., GitHub Actions or ArgoCD) as well as modern frontend architecture patterns. Practical awareness of common frontend security risks, including XSS and CSRF, and how to design against them. Strong working fluency with agentic coding tools and spec-driven development workflows, including specification writing, code generation, test generation, and critical review. Clear communication, with the ability to articulate technical concepts and trade-offs in plain English. High ambition and a strong sense of urgency, with the drive to deliver an ambitious product roadmap at pace using AI, and a positive, can-do attitude.Experience and Qualifications 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including 5+ years of commercial React and TypeScript. Experience shipping and operating production frontends for customer-facing SaaS products, including monitoring, incident response, and performance improvement. Experience working in a large, long-lived codebase where design patterns, testability, and maintainability genuinely matter. Experience consuming and shaping REST APIs in a service-oriented architecture, ideally backed by Django REST Framework or an equivalent. Experience working in cross-functional teams with product managers and designers on shared customer outcomes, not only technical delivery. Experience using AI coding tools in a professional software delivery workflow, ideally within a spec-driven development framework. title: Product Marketing Manager, Energy & Defence
description: Finance Deserves Better Finance teams at fast-growing companies run global, real-time businesses on a patchwork of legacy ERPs and point solutions. Every new entity, project or tool adds another system to stitch together and another hire to keep the numbers reconciled. Light gives them a way out. We build the finance solution that lets finance teams have it all, through three parts that work as one: Our ledger records every transaction across every entity in real time, so the numbers hold up from day one. Our apps adapt Light to how each business runs, from procurement to billing to reporting. Our agents operate the repetitive work that used to need another hire, so finance teams spend their time on the decisions that matter. Today we run the finance function for companies like Lovable, Legora and Keyshot, with backing from Atomico, Balderton, Seedcamp, Cherry and Entrée. Now we’re taking Light into specific industries, with the ambition of becoming the operating layer each one runs on. Energy and defence sit among our priority sectors. The Role We’re looking for a Product Marketing Manager to go deep on energy and defence and work out how Light wins there. Energy developers, operators and service businesses share a lot with defence technology and service suppliers. Both run on project and contract economics, both report across several entities, and both face long, multi-stakeholder buying cycles where auditability and approvals carry real weight. Your job is to understand these buyers better than anyone at Light, turn what you learn into positioning and proof our sales team can use, and build the playbook we follow to scale our go-to-market across both sectors. You’ll sit in our product marketing team and work side by side with the Sales Managers who cover these sectors, with support from demand generation, field marketing and product. What You’ll Be Doing Interviewing customers, prospects and specialist partners to learn how energy and defence businesses buy, what makes them change and where their finance workflows break. Mapping the market with Sales: which segments we go after first, which we test, and which we leave for later. Turning what you learn into positioning, messaging and competitive arguments that hold up in front of a project director or a CFO. Building the sales kit, from customer stories and demo narratives to objection handling and one-pagers, so our reps speak each sector’s language. Training sales reps and SDRs on the buyers, procurement cycles, contract structures and regulatory context of each segment, and joining customer calls to hear what lands. Bringing the sectors’ requirements back to Product, from project and contract economics to cash visibility, evidence trails and integrations with operational systems, and separating the needs that recur from the one-off requests. Giving demand generation and field marketing the insight, content and angles they need for sector campaigns and events, and tracking what turns into pipeline. Writing down what works, so the next sector we enter starts from a playbook rather than a blank page. What We Think* You’ll Need Product marketing experience at a B2B SaaS company, with a track record of taking a product or segment from insight to launch to sales adoption. A habit of talking to customers, and the judgement to turn interviews into clear positioning. Experience in energy, defence, infrastructure, industrials or another complex B2B sector helps. Curiosity and the speed to earn credibility with technical buyers matter more. Strong writing, from a sharp one-pager to a customer story people want to share. Comfort working with Sales every day, and a feel for what helps a rep win a long, complex deal. An analytical streak. You can read funnel data, spot where deals stall and test why. Daily use of AI for research, writing and analysis, with the discipline to check what it tells you. A can-do, empathetic and collaborative spirit. No brilliant jerks here, please. *If the core of the role sounds compelling but you don’t tick every box, we’d still love for you to reach out and convince us you’re the right person. The Good Stuff 🏢 A five-day, in-office culture with a high-density team in London. 💸 A competitive salary and potential stock options. 🏝 25 days of annual leave plus UK public holidays. 🥳 Regular socials and two company offsites a year. The last 2 were in Tuscany & Provence! 🌍 Travel to Copenhagen, Munich, New York, Paris and wherever energy and defence customers, partners and industry events take us. 🚀 The chance to define how Light wins in two sectors from their first deals. Light is an equal opportunity employer. The Famous Last Words Energy and defence businesses manage complex projects, contracts and entities on finance tools that weren’t built for them. We want to change that, and we want you to learn both sectors inside out and show us how. When you apply, tell us about a segment you got to know from scratch: how you learned it, what you changed because of it, and how you helped Sales win there. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background.
